relations.note: Soil-water and ice-growth premises support editorial soil-physics placement.

original_record.card: One degree Brix corresponds to one gram of sucrose per 100 grams of a sucrose-and-water solution. In fruit juice, a refractometer reports soluble solids on this scale, so the reading need not isolate sucrose from other dissolved substances.

evidence.locator: Table 4, definitions of sample parameters; line 1242
evidence.note: Sucrose scale measures fruit-juice soluble solids by refractometer.

original_record.label: Degrees Brix
original_record.learning_takeaway: A sucrose-calibrated scale helps compare soluble solids in fruit juice.

relations.note: Refractometer use supports an editorial refractive-index application.

original_record.card: Deprescribing is supervised medication discontinuation or dose reduction after reviewing appropriateness, benefits and risks with the patient. It requires continued monitoring: withdrawal symptoms or recurrence of the original problem can lead to dose adjustment or restarting. Reducing medication is an ongoing clinical decision.

evidence.locator: Definition and steps; lines 132-142; ongoing monitoring; line 169
evidence.note: Supervised shared decisions require monitoring for withdrawal or recurrence.

original_record.label: Deprescribing
original_record.learning_takeaway: Supervised medication reduction requires reviewing benefit, risk and subsequent symptoms.

relations.note: Clinical medication-management premises support an editorial medicine application.

original_record.card: In classical projective geometry, two triangles are perspective from a point when lines joining corresponding vertices meet there. Desargues' theorem links this to a line: the intersections of corresponding sides are collinear, connecting two different kinds of geometric alignment.

evidence.locator: Theorem statement; lines 16-19

original_record.label: Desargues' theorem
original_record.learning_takeaway: Triangles sharing a center of perspectivity produce collinear intersections of corresponding sides.

relations.note: Projective incidence premises support editorial projective-geometry placement.

original_record.card: Design ease is additional garment fullness chosen for style, beyond the room needed for comfortable wear. This extra allowance shapes the garment's outline; a pattern can combine comfort room with deliberately chosen styling.

evidence.locator: Wearing versus design ease; fabric edges; lines 84, 154, 178
evidence.note: Additional pattern fullness serves garment style.

original_record.label: Design ease
original_record.learning_takeaway: Extra room beyond wearing ease shapes a garment's outline and fullness.

relations.note: Guide explicitly defines a sewing-pattern styling component.

original_record.card: Desirable difficulties are learning conditions that can make practice feel harder while improving later retention or transfer. Their value depends on the learner being able to overcome them. Immediate fluency therefore gives an incomplete picture of lasting learning.

evidence.locator: Opening definition, PDF p. 1, lines 1-11; Why Desirable Difficulties Are Desirable, PDF pp. 3-4, lines 60-71

original_record.label: Desirable difficulties
original_record.learning_takeaway: Some practice conditions slow immediate performance while improving later retention or transfer.

relations.note: The author explicitly frames desirable difficulties as learning conditions affecting retention and transfer.

original_record.card: Dhikr is devotional remembrance in Sufism, often performed through rhythmic recitation of God’s names or litanies. Some forms include poetry, dance or instruments. The repeated vocal pattern organizes worship, while the varying accompaniments show that remembrance has several forms of expression.

evidence.locator: Definition, line 56

original_record.label: Dhikr
original_record.learning_takeaway: Recognize repeated remembrance across varied devotional forms.

relations.note: The definition explicitly identifies dhikr as Sufi devotion.

original_record.card: Dispersion measure sums the free-electron density along a radio signal's path. For pulsars, this electron column determines frequency-dependent arrival delays: lower-frequency waves arrive later. It characterizes the intervening sightline, rather than being an intrinsic property of the pulsar.

evidence.locator: Section 6.2 Pulsars and the Interstellar Medium; equations 6.43–6.46 and following text; lines 241-255
evidence.note: Integrated electron column controls frequency-dependent propagation delay.

original_record.label: Dispersion measure
original_record.learning_takeaway: Radio pulse delays encode an integrated column of electrons along the line of sight.

relations.note: Radio-propagation premises support editorial radio-astronomy placement.
Pulsar signals measure the intervening electron column.

original_record.card: A double dactyl is light verse in two four-line stanzas. Most lines contain two feet, each with a stressed syllable followed by two unstressed ones. Nonsense, a person’s name, one six-syllable word and shorter rhyming endings create a compact compositional puzzle.

evidence.locator: Opening instructional paragraphs, lines 0–3
Dactyl entry, line 94

original_record.label: Double dactyl
original_record.learning_takeaway: Fit comic content to rhythm and a single long word.

relations.note: The university instructional page identifies this as a verse form.

original_record.card: Dryeration separates corn drying from final cooling. Hot corn rests in a cooling bin before air is introduced; retained heat helps remove additional moisture during cooling. Using that remaining heat makes the cooling stage part of drying rather than only temperature reduction.

evidence.locator: Increased capacity and efficiency; Process; lines 263-290
evidence.note: Tempering and slow cooling use retained corn heat for drying.

original_record.label: Dryeration
original_record.learning_takeaway: Corn's retained heat supports extra drying after a resting period and slow cooling.

relations.note: Guide explicitly identifies a corn-drying method.

original_record.card: The Duckworth–Lewis–Stern method adjusts targets in interrupted limited-overs cricket. ICC uses a Stern Edition calculator; its published Standard Edition fallback explains resources through overs remaining and wickets lost. Edition matters when interpreting the published target-adjustment methodology.

evidence.locator: Duckworth Lewis Stern introduction, lines 9-14
Opening status statement and section 1, PDF p. 1, lines 1-20

original_record.label: Duckworth–Lewis–Stern method
original_record.learning_takeaway: DLS revises targets when a limited-overs cricket match is interrupted; the historical Standard Edition models overs and wickets as scoring resources.

relations.note: ICC explicitly describes its adopted DLS method for interrupted cricket matches.

original_record.card: Duration neglect describes evaluations that give an experience’s length little weight even when its duration is known. Fredrickson and Kahneman studied brief affective episodes; remembered evaluations did not simply track elapsed time. Their finding does not automatically extend to experiences lasting months.

evidence.locator: General Discussion, PDF p. 10, lines 1029-1033, 1057-1070

original_record.label: Duration neglect
original_record.learning_takeaway: Remembered evaluations of brief experiences can give duration little weight even when duration is known.

relations.note: The study’s remembered-experience evaluations establish the factual memory connection; memory is an editorial parent.

original_record.card: Dutch roll is a coupled oscillation in an aircraft’s rolling and yawing motion. Depending on its lateral and directional stability, the motion may be weakly damped. Some aircraft use a yaw damper to reduce this recurring side-to-side motion.

evidence.locator: Chapter 5, Free Directional Oscillations (Dutch Roll), printed p. 5-20 / PDF p. 20

original_record.label: Dutch roll
original_record.learning_takeaway: Coupled roll and yaw oscillations can have weak damping and may require yaw dampers.

relations.note: This mode is explicitly taught within the handbook’s Aerodynamics of Flight chapter.

original_record.card: The margin of appreciation is discretion allowed to national authorities in European human rights review. They initially assess a restriction’s necessity, but the Court can review their decision. Its breadth varies with the issues and interests involved, so discretion does not settle legality.

evidence.locator: Is the interference necessary in a democratic society?, paragraphs 34–36, printed pages 15–16

original_record.label: Margin of appreciation (European human-rights law)
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect national discretion with continuing judicial review.

relations.note: Article 8 review permits qualified national discretion.

original_record.card: The pilot judgment procedure lets the European Court of Human Rights address structural problems behind repetitive applications. It selects representative cases and indicates remedial measures to governments. Related cases may be paused while national action proceeds, with examination resumable when justice requires.

evidence.locator: What is the pilot judgment procedure?, printed page 1, lines 4–18

original_record.label: Pilot judgment procedure (European Court of Human Rights)
original_record.learning_takeaway: Link individual cases with remedies for a systemic problem.

relations.note: Pilot judgments address systemic violations of Convention rights.

original_record.card: Elysia chlorotica is a sea slug that retains chloroplasts from Vaucheria litorea. In a laboratory study, juveniles fed for seven days kept plastids after food removal, whereas earlier removal led to plastid breakdown. Stable retention develops during early feeding.

evidence.locator: Abstract; Introduction; Figure 1; lines 143-173
evidence.note: Laboratory feeding duration affected plastid stability.

original_record.label: Elysia chlorotica
original_record.learning_takeaway: This sea slug stabilizes ingested plastids during an early developmental feeding period.

relations.note: Source explicitly identifies a sea slug.

original_record.card: An ephemeron pairs a key with a value during garbage collection. The value is retained only when the key is reachable without depending on that value. A value’s reference back to its key therefore cannot, by itself, keep the pair alive.
original_record.label: Ephemeron
original_record.learning_takeaway: Conditional retention by a separately reachable key avoids keeping key/value cycles alive.

relations.note: Editorial learning parent: Racket’s garbage-collection reachability construct belongs within computer science.

original_record.card: Epoch-based reclamation delays freeing objects removed from a concurrent structure. Readers pin the current epoch while accessing it. Retired objects wait until readers that could still hold references have finished, separating logical removal from safe memory reuse.

evidence.locator: Description; Pinning; Garbage, lines 29-42

original_record.label: Epoch-based memory reclamation
original_record.learning_takeaway: Epochs and pinned readers delay destruction until no earlier reader can reference retired nodes.

relations.note: Epoch-and-pinning reclamation differs from general concurrency and individual hazard pointers.

original_record.card: Equal Earth is a world-map projection that preserves relative areas while distorting shapes, angles, and distances. This makes it useful for thematic maps comparing area characteristics: a region’s mapped size remains meaningful even when its outline changes.

evidence.locator: Description; Distortion; Usage

original_record.label: Equal Earth projection
original_record.learning_takeaway: Compare areas without mistaking preserved size for preserved shape.

relations.note: Esri explicitly identifies Equal Earth as a map projection.

aliases: European Train Control System braking curve
original_record.card: ETCS braking curves predict how a train’s speed should change with distance toward a restriction. The calculation combines train braking characteristics with track data. These curves support speed supervision; their predicted trajectory is a model, not an exact realized stopping distance.

evidence.locator: Introduction and braking-curve prediction description, lines 15-21

original_record.label: ETCS braking curve
original_record.learning_takeaway: A train-and-track model predicts speed against distance so ETCS can supervise braking toward a limit.

relations.note: The source explicitly describes braking-curve computation as part of ETCS speed-and-position supervision.

original_record.card: Euclidean buffering draws a distance zone using straight-line measurements on a flat coordinate plane. It works best around features concentrated within a suitably projected small region. Where the projection distorts distance substantially, equal map offsets no longer represent equal distances on Earth.

evidence.locator: “Euclidean and geodesic buffering”, method bullets and shape-preserving Geodesic option

original_record.label: Euclidean buffering
original_record.learning_takeaway: Identify when flat-map distance zones inherit projection distortion.

relations.note: Esri names Euclidean buffering as a geographic buffer construction method.

original_record.card: Event Segmentation Theory proposes that people use ongoing models to predict what happens next. A temporary rise in prediction error signals an event boundary and updates processing. The account connects perceived divisions in continuous activity with attention and memory.

evidence.locator: Abstract; A Theory of Event Segmentation, lines 94-113

original_record.label: Event Segmentation Theory
original_record.learning_takeaway: Transient prediction errors mark perceived event boundaries in the proposed account of ongoing activity.

relations.note: The authors explicitly frame the theory as an account of perceptual boundaries in continuous activity.

original_record.card: Ferrar Glacier carries ice from Taylor Dome toward Antarctica's Ross Sea. Snow accumulating at the dome compresses into ice, some of which flows through this glacier and the Royal Society Range. The named route connects inland accumulation with ice reaching the coast.

evidence.locator: Snow accumulation and ice route; lines 268-270
evidence.note: Taylor Dome accumulation supplies the named glacier's seaward route.

original_record.label: Ferrar Glacier
original_record.learning_takeaway: A named glacier connects inland snow accumulation with an ice-flow route toward the sea.

relations.note: NASA explicitly describes Ferrar as a river of ice.

original_record.card: Fitting-attitude theories explain value through responses that an object merits. Being admirable, for example, is explained through the fittingness of admiration. The claim concerns appropriate responses, not whatever people happen to feel, so actual affection or dislike alone does not settle an object’s value.

evidence.locator: Introduction, lines 13–20

original_record.label: Fitting-attitude theories of value
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish a deserved response from an actual feeling.

relations.note: The entry explicitly presents these as theories explaining value.

original_record.card: Focal closure occurs when two people sharing an activity or organization form a social tie. The shared focus supplies a setting for contact. In a social-affiliation network, the resulting edge connects people.

evidence.locator: 4.3, Co-Evolution of Social and Affiliation Networks, PDF p. 12, lines 370-374

original_record.label: Focal closure
original_record.learning_takeaway: A shared activity can help create a friendship.

relations.note: Shared affiliations can create a social tie.

original_record.card: The friendship paradox reflects sampling through social ties. People with many friends appear in more people’s friend lists, so they are overrepresented among friends. Average friend counts can consequently be higher in this sample; the statement concerns sampling rather than every individual.

evidence.locator: Abstract, lines 46-48

original_record.label: Friendship paradox
original_record.learning_takeaway: Sampling people through friendship links overrepresents people who have many friends.

relations.note: The original abstract explicitly explains comparisons of friend counts in a social network through disproportionate exposure to highly connected friends.

original_record.card: Frost heave raises ground as ice grows within freezing soil, sometimes deforming road surfaces. Growing ice layers can draw in additional water that freezes, enlarging the layer. The movement therefore need not result solely from expansion of water already occupying soil pores.

evidence.locator: Density of frozen water and cryosuction; lines 89-94
evidence.note: Ice growth and additional water can heave frozen ground.

original_record.label: Frost heave
original_record.learning_takeaway: Growing ice in soil can raise the ground and deform a road surface.

relations.note: Soil-water and ice-growth premises support editorial soil-physics placement.

original_record.card: Gamelan gong kebyar is a Balinese ensemble style that emerged in northern Bali around 1915. Rapid tempo changes and dynamic interlocking parts distinguish its repertoire. An album labeled court music illustrates a contextual trap: most documented performances belonged to other settings.

evidence.locator: David Harnish’s guest article, lines 450–468

original_record.label: Gamelan gong kebyar
original_record.learning_takeaway: Hear musical dynamics while checking performance context.

relations.note: Gong kebyar is identified as a gamelan style.

original_record.card: Gathering draws a longer length of fabric into small folds so it fits a shorter attaching edge. In a machine-sewn ruffle, long stitches provide threads that can be pulled and adjusted. Distributing the folds lets the ruffle fit its band.

evidence.locator: Gathering stitches and ruffle attachment; lines 317-336
evidence.note: Pulled gathering threads fit a ruffle to its band.

original_record.label: Gathering in sewing
original_record.learning_takeaway: Draw longer cloth into small folds so it fits a shorter attaching edge.

relations.note: Source explicitly gathers a ruffle in a sewing project.

original_record.card: Generating a word from a cue can leave a stronger memory than reading it. The generation effect emerged in experiments comparing those encoding conditions, with advantages in later recognition and recall. Its size and occurrence depend on the study conditions.

evidence.locator: Original abstract summary and author retrospective, single PDF page, lines 3-8 and 26-43

original_record.label: Generation effect
original_record.learning_takeaway: Generating a word can improve later memory compared with reading the same word.

relations.note: The author describes the original experiments as comparisons of memory for generated and read words.

original_record.card: Geodesic buffering builds distance zones while accounting for Earth’s curved spheroidal surface. It is useful over large extents and near poles or the date line. A zone may look distorted on a flat map while showing the intended distance correctly on a globe.

evidence.locator: “Euclidean and geodesic buffering”, method bullets and shape-preserving Geodesic option

original_record.label: Geodesic buffering
original_record.learning_takeaway: Separate curved-surface distance from flat-map appearance.

relations.note: Esri names geodesic buffering as a geographic buffer construction method.

original_record.card: In an amorphous polymer, the glass transition marks a temperature range where chain segments gain substantial mobility. The material changes from glassy behavior toward rubbery behavior. This differs from melting crystalline regions: segment movement and crystalline order describe different changes.

evidence.locator: Long-range segmental motion; Glass Transition vs. Melting; lines 25-26 and 51-56
evidence.note: Segmental mobility changes; crystalline melting is distinguished.

original_record.label: Glass transition
original_record.learning_takeaway: Amorphous polymer segment motion changes across a temperature range, separately from crystalline melting.

relations.note: Source explicitly explains a polymer transition.

original_record.card: GN-z11 is a distant galaxy seen about 430 million years after the Big Bang. NASA's 2024 Webb report describes extended host-galaxy light and a compact central source. Its colors and gas signatures support a black-hole interpretation, illustrating how indirect observations investigate early galaxies.

evidence.locator: Host galaxy and compact source; lines 322-336
evidence.note: Dated report resolves host and compact source with black-hole evidence.

original_record.label: GN-z11
original_record.learning_takeaway: Resolve host-galaxy light from a compact source to investigate an early galaxy's unusual brightness.

relations.note: NASA explicitly identifies GN-z11 and its host component as a galaxy.

original_record.card: For a spherical Earth, Goode homolosine combines sinusoidal and Mollweide projections to preserve areas. Its familiar interrupted versions split the map into lobes emphasizing land or oceans. These cuts reduce the shape distortion found near the edges of its uninterrupted form.

evidence.locator: Description; Graticule; Usage; Limitations

original_record.label: Goode homolosine projection
original_record.learning_takeaway: Understand how interruptions trade continuity for reduced shape distortion.

relations.note: Esri identifies Goode homolosine as a map projection.

original_record.card: Grainline in woven fabric follows its threads, whose lengthwise and crosswise directions should meet at right angles. A printed stripe can be off grain. Aligning pieces by the print alone may therefore produce difficulties when matching patterns or cutting straight pieces.

evidence.locator: Checking fabric grain and printing; lines 69-73
evidence.note: Thread grain differs from printed design alignment.

original_record.label: Grainline in woven fabric
original_record.learning_takeaway: Thread direction, rather than a printed stripe, determines whether fabric is on grain.

relations.note: Cutting-alignment premises support an editorial sewing facet.

original_record.card: Guard cells occur in pairs around a stoma, an opening in a plant's surface. By opening that pore, they let gases pass between the surrounding air and deeper leaf cells. The cells and the opening are distinct structures.

evidence.locator: Dermal tissue; lines 224-226
evidence.note: Paired cells open stomata for gas exchange.

original_record.label: Guard cell
original_record.learning_takeaway: Paired guard cells control an opening used for leaf gas exchange.

relations.note: Passage locates guard cells around stomata.

original_record.card: Gyotaku transfers a fish’s surface to paper by rubbing it over an inked specimen. The print records details of shape and texture. In a Smithsonian educational version, rubber replicas replace real fish; excessive paint blurs the transfer, making material quantity part of the result.

evidence.locator: Catherine Sutera’s museum account, lines 65–69

original_record.label: Gyotaku
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect transferred detail with paint quantity and surface contact.

relations.note: Documented ink and paper transfer supports this printmaking placement.

original_record.card: Haibun combines prose and haiku, a literary form originating in Japan. The prose often describes an environment and precedes a poem whose connection remains implicit. In Bashō’s travel writing, the surrounding narrative and individual haiku create meaning together without spelling out every link.

evidence.locator: Definition; “From A Poet’s Glossary”, prose–haiku relationship

original_record.label: Haibun
original_record.learning_takeaway: Read prose and haiku through their implicit connection.

relations.note: The Academy identifies haibun as a literary poetic form.

original_record.card: A halocline is a layer where salinity changes rapidly with depth. Fresher surface water over saltier water can create one. It describes a salt gradient, while a pycnocline describes density and a thermocline describes temperature; these layers need not coincide.

evidence.locator: Main pycnocline and salinity layers; PDF page 2 (zero-based 1), lines 145-179
evidence.note: Ocean salinity-gradient layer distinguished from density and temperature layers.

original_record.label: Halocline
original_record.learning_takeaway: A salinity gradient can separate fresher surface water from saltier deep water.

relations.note: Source explicitly describes a salinity-stratified ocean zone.

original_record.card: A single plane can simultaneously divide each of three finite-volume solids in three-dimensional space into equal volumes. The ham sandwich theorem extends this pattern: in n dimensions, one hyperplane can bisect n finite volumes, however differently they are positioned.

evidence.locator: Theorem statement and three-dimensional argument; lines 13-20
evidence.note: Simultaneous finite-volume bisection in matching dimension.

original_record.label: Ham sandwich theorem
original_record.learning_takeaway: One plane can simultaneously bisect three three-dimensional volumes.

relations.note: Dimension and continuous-volume premises support editorial topology placement.

original_record.card: The Japanese Hayabusa2 mission collected samples from asteroid Ryugu and returned them to Earth in 2020. Its instruments and small rovers explored the surface. Returning material lets laboratory analysis complement spacecraft observations, giving researchers physical asteroid samples to examine directly.

evidence.locator: Mission overview, sample return and craft design; lines 241, 264, 304-312
evidence.note: Ryugu exploration and completed 2020 sample return.

original_record.label: Hayabusa2
original_record.learning_takeaway: Returning physical asteroid samples lets laboratory analysis complement spacecraft observations.

relations.note: Sampling and return support editorial space-exploration placement.
NASA explicitly names an asteroid as the mission's study target.

original_record.card: A hazard pointer lets a thread announce that it is protecting an object in concurrent memory. Removed objects are retired before reclamation. Checking published hazard pointers delays freeing protected objects, separating removal from safe reuse of their memory.

evidence.locator: 2 Hazard pointer overview, PDF pp. 4-5, lines 125-162

original_record.label: Hazard pointer
original_record.learning_takeaway: Reclaim nodes removed from lock-free objects for safe later reuse.

relations.note: Concurrent computing is broader than this named memory-reclamation methodology.

original_record.card: In Fricker’s account, hermeneutical injustice arises when unequal shared interpretive resources leave someone unfairly unable to understand a social experience. Sexual harassment before that concept gained recognition illustrates the problem: the obstacle lies partly in collective understanding, rather than only one listener’s disbelief.

evidence.locator: Printed page 1, hermeneutical-injustice definition and harassment example

original_record.label: Hermeneutical injustice
original_record.learning_takeaway: Locate an interpretive obstacle within unequal shared resources.

relations.note: Fricker explicitly identifies this form of epistemic injustice.

original_record.card: Homophily is the tendency for social ties to connect similar people. Shared traits can shape who meets whom and who forms a friendship. It describes a population pattern, allowing many individual ties between unlike people.

evidence.locator: 4.1 Homophily, PDF pp. 2-3, lines 23-45 and 64-78

original_record.label: Homophily
original_record.learning_takeaway: Shared traits often accompany social ties.

relations.note: Similarity among connected people in social networks.

original_record.card: Hotine oblique Mercator aligns a conformal map with a region extending diagonally rather than north–south or east–west. It preserves angles and shapes locally, but area and distance distortion increase away from the central region. Orientation therefore matters when choosing a regional projection.

evidence.locator: Description; Distortion; Usage; Variants

original_record.label: Hotine oblique Mercator projection
original_record.learning_takeaway: Match a conformal projection to an oblique region.

relations.note: Esri identifies Hotine oblique Mercator as a map projection.

original_record.card: HTTP Message Signatures authenticate selected request or response components and accompanying signature metadata. The signer builds a defined signature base from those covered parts. Verification therefore concerns the named coverage; it does not automatically authenticate every field or every message byte.

evidence.locator: Abstract; section 3, line 1399; 1.1 Terminology; 7.3.3 Symmetric Cryptography, official text companion lines 254-276 and 3267-3287

original_record.label: HTTP Message Signatures
original_record.learning_takeaway: A signature verifies the chosen covered HTTP components and associated signature metadata.

relations.note: The RFC applies digital signatures to HTTP signature bases; its symmetric-MAC option lies outside this digital-signature parent.

original_record.card: An HTTP Structured Fields dictionary is an ordered collection of unique textual keys and typed values. Values may be individual items or inner lists. A field specification gives those keys meaning, letting a common parser handle the representation.

evidence.locator: 3 Structured Data Types, lines 252-259; 3.2 Dictionaries, lines 330-336; 2.4 compatibility, lines 243-246

original_record.label: HTTP structured field dictionary
original_record.learning_takeaway: HTTP field dictionaries map unique textual keys to typed items or inner lists.

relations.note: The specification explicitly defines Dictionaries as a top-level representation for HTTP fields.

original_record.card: Complementarity gives the International Criminal Court a role alongside national criminal justice. Under the inspected Rome Statute, genuine domestic investigation or prosecution can make a case inadmissible. Proceedings that shield a suspect illustrate unwillingness; other jurisdiction and admissibility conditions also apply.

evidence.locator: Preamble, Article 1, Article 17 (lines 18, 25, 244–258)

original_record.label: Complementarity (International Criminal Court)
original_record.learning_takeaway: Evaluate genuine domestic proceedings before ICC admissibility.

relations.note: Articles 1 and 17 establish the ICC’s complementary role.

original_record.card: The Ignatian Examen is Christian prayer through reflection on daily experience. One adapted sequence begins with awareness of God, reviews gratitude and emotions, then prays over one feature of the day and looks toward tomorrow. Ordinary events become material for discernment.

evidence.locator: Main explanation and five-step method, lines 85–98

original_record.label: Ignatian Examen
original_record.learning_takeaway: Use daily events as material for reflective prayer.

relations.note: The source describes an adapted Christian prayer method.

original_record.card: The illusion of explanatory depth occurs when a feeling of understanding exceeds one’s ability to explain a mechanism. Attempting a detailed explanation can expose gaps and lower confidence. In the experiments, this gap was especially apparent for explanatory understanding.

evidence.locator: Abstract and Introduction, PDF pp. 1-2, lines 8-17 and 54-65; discussion of recalibration after explanation, PDF p. 15, lines 482-487

original_record.label: Illusion of explanatory depth
original_record.learning_takeaway: Trying to explain a mechanism can reveal gaps hidden by an initial feeling of understanding.

relations.note: The authors identify the explanatory-knowledge illusion as a metacognitive problem and test changes in self-ratings of understanding.

original_record.card: In an observational treatment study, people classified as treated may need to survive from cohort entry until treatment begins. Misassigning that pre-treatment period to the treated group can create an apparent survival advantage unrelated to the treatment's effect.

evidence.locator: Immortal time bias; lines 204-206
evidence.note: Survival required before exposure assignment can produce spurious benefit.

original_record.label: Immortal time bias
original_record.learning_takeaway: Survival needed to receive an exposure can create a misleading apparent treatment advantage.

relations.note: Source explicitly defines bias through cohort-entry and intervention timing.

original_record.card: Inattentional blindness occurs when an unexpected visible event escapes awareness while attention is directed elsewhere. In Simons and Chabris’s counting task, some observers missed a conspicuous person crossing the scene. Detection varied with what observers attended to.

evidence.locator: Abstract and Introduction, PDF pp. 1-2, lines 32-56; Procedures and Results, PDF pp. 8-11

original_record.label: Inattentional blindness
original_record.learning_takeaway: Attention to a monitoring task can leave a visible unexpected event unnoticed.

relations.note: The original authors explicitly study inattentional blindness as a form of visual perception without focused attention.

original_record.card: Takuo Itoh’s 1995 furisode kimono demonstrates shibori at the scale of an entire garment. A continuous dyed pattern crosses the back seam and extends from body to sleeves. Planning on fabric of fixed width aligns areas that garment construction later joins.

evidence.locator: Curatorial description, lines 10–12; object identification, 31–39

original_record.label: Tokuseu Hitome Sohshibori Hon Furisode (Met 1997.228)
original_record.learning_takeaway: Trace a planned dye pattern across garment seams.

relations.note: The museum explicitly identifies this garment’s shibori technique.

aliases: Peremptory norms of general international law
original_record.card: Jus cogens denotes peremptory norms accepted by the international community of states as a whole, permitting no derogation. Under Vienna Convention Article 53, a treaty conflicting with such a norm when concluded is void; ordinary agreement cannot override it.

evidence.locator: Article 53, printed page 17

original_record.label: Jus cogens
original_record.learning_takeaway: Recognize limits on treaty agreement.

relations.note: Peremptory norms constrain international law.

original_record.card: Kanoko shibori is a resist dyeing method that binds small pinches of cloth before dyeing. Releasing the ties produces tiny undyed details, often squares with central dots. A Met robe illustrates how many individually tied units create an extensive patterned surface.

evidence.locator: Curatorial description, lines 10–11; Artwork Details

original_record.label: Kanoko shibori
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect individual bindings with a repeated dot pattern.

relations.note: The Met describes kanoko as a shibori variant.

original_record.card: Khipus recorded information in the Inca Empire through cords and knots. Knot positions can represent decimal places, while twists, attachments, and colors provide further distinctions whose meanings scholars investigate. Numerical organization therefore depends on a cord’s structure, rather than an alphabetic sequence of written words.

evidence.locator: What is a khipu?; Encoding the Khipu; Khipu Uses, lines 132–157 and 195

original_record.label: Khipu
original_record.learning_takeaway: Read decimal organization in knots while retaining interpretive uncertainty.

relations.note: NIST documents khipu use throughout the Inca Empire.

original_record.card: Kintsugi is the Japanese art of repairing broken ceramics with gold lacquer. The repair restores function while giving damage a visible artistic role. The Met interprets this treatment as enhancing a prized object’s value, a curatorial judgment rather than a universal price rule.

evidence.locator: Exhibition overview, lines 10–11

original_record.label: Kintsugi
original_record.learning_takeaway: Understand visible repair as an artistic treatment of damage.

relations.note: The exhibition identifies kintsugi within Japanese ceramic art.

original_record.card: Kleptoplasty is a symbiosis in which an animal retains chloroplasts taken from algal food. In Elysia chlorotica, these plastids remain in digestive cells and continue photosynthesis; the slug retains chloroplasts rather than complete algal cells.

evidence.locator: Abstract; Introduction; Figure 1; lines 143-173

original_record.label: Kleptoplasty
original_record.learning_takeaway: An animal can retain algal chloroplasts without retaining a complete algal cell.

relations.note: Introduction explicitly identifies plastid symbiosis.

original_record.card: A koan is a paradoxical question that a Zen teacher gives a student for meditation. Its purpose is to interrupt habitual analytical thinking rather than supply an ordinary explanatory answer. The tradition treats this encounter as a possible route toward realization.

evidence.locator: Definition, line 56

original_record.label: Koan
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish a contemplative question from an explanatory answer.

relations.note: Zen meditation context motivates this Buddhist practice placement.

original_record.card: Kotekan is an interlocking technique in Balinese gamelan. Two musicians divide rapid melodic figures into separate parts whose combination maintains rhythmic continuity. The result belongs to the composition’s melody: listening to either player alone misses the continuous composite line.

evidence.locator: Paragraph 2.2, lines 67–70

original_record.label: Kotekan
original_record.learning_takeaway: Hear the composite melody across paired parts.

relations.note: Tenzer identifies kotekan within Balinese gamelan texture.

original_record.card: Kulintang Kultura honors musician and teacher Danongan Kalanduyan through two contrasting discs. His ensemble performs traditional Philippine gong music on the first; diaspora artists combine kulintang with contemporary genres on the second. Their juxtaposition makes musical inheritance and transformation audible within one collection.

evidence.locator: Album description, lines 456–457; Release Info, 505–513

original_record.label: Kulintang Kultura: Danongan Kalanduyan and Gong Music of the Philippine Diaspora
original_record.learning_takeaway: Compare inheritance and transformation across the album’s discs.

relations.note: The album documents traditional and diaspora kulintang music.

original_record.card: Kulintang is a gong chime music tradition of the Philippines. The Kulintang Kultura album contrasts traditional ensemble repertoire with diaspora musicians’ combinations of kulintang and electronic, hip hop, rock and jazz styles. Hearing both reveals preservation through changing musical arrangements.

evidence.locator: Lesson introduction and learning objectives, lines 440–455
Album description, lines 456–457
evidence.note: Traditional and contemporary repertoire comparison inspected.

original_record.label: Kulintang music
original_record.learning_takeaway: Compare traditional repertoire with diaspora adaptations.

relations.note: The lesson identifies kulintang as Philippine gong chime music.

original_record.card: Kundiman is a Filipino song form in triple meter. In Felipe De Leon’s account, flowing melodies and subtle second beat syncopation loosen the beat’s pull. Devotion can address a partner, family, spiritual figure or motherland, extending the form beyond romantic love.

evidence.locator: Essay adaptation, lines 68–78

original_record.label: Kundiman
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect triple meter and melodic flow with devotion.

relations.note: The essay identifies kundiman as a musical form.

original_record.card: LAGEOS is a pair of passive satellites covered with reflecting prisms. Laser measurements to these orbiting targets help investigate Earth's motion and shape, including plate movement and rotation. The satellites carry no electronics or sensors: their role is to provide stable reflective targets.

evidence.locator: LAGEOS 1 & 2 overview; lines 235-258
evidence.note: Passive reflecting satellite pair supports laser geodesy.

original_record.label: LAGEOS
original_record.learning_takeaway: Passive reflecting satellites provide long-lived laser targets for measuring Earth's motion and shape.

relations.note: NASA explicitly identifies a pair of orbiting satellites.

original_record.card: Leaf area index compares green leaf surface with ground area. For broadleaf plants it uses one leaf side; for conifers it uses half the total needle surface. This canopy measure helps model photosynthesis and exchanges of water, energy and carbon.

evidence.locator: Leaf Area Index definition and uses; lines 50-54
evidence.note: Leaf-surface ratio and plant-process modeling uses are explicit.

original_record.label: Leaf area index
original_record.learning_takeaway: Normalize leaf surface by ground area to describe canopy structure and model vegetation processes.

relations.note: Canopy and plant-process premises support editorial plant-physiology placement.

original_record.card: Cancer screening disproportionately detects slower-growing cancers because they remain detectable before symptoms for longer. This length-time bias changes the mix of cancers found. More early-stage diagnoses can therefore occur without establishing that screening reduces deaths; detection patterns alone do not show the benefit.

evidence.locator: Length bias and overdiagnosis; lines 34-38
evidence.note: Longer preclinical windows enrich slower cancers and distort benefit measures.

original_record.label: Length-time bias in cancer screening
original_record.learning_takeaway: Screening preferentially detects slower-growing cancers with longer preclinical windows.

relations.note: Source explicitly explains the bias in cancer screening.

original_record.card: L’Estampe Originale was a print portfolio issued in nine installments from 1893 to 1895. Its range of media depended on collaboration between artists and professional printers. These partnerships enabled technical experiments, making the printer’s expertise part of artistic production.

evidence.locator: Curatorial article, lines 13–16, 22, 31–38

original_record.label: L’Estampe Originale
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect artistic experimentation with professional printers’ expertise.

relations.note: The portfolio collected collaborative experimental printmaking.

original_record.card: Under FIVB 2025–2028 rules, the Libero replaces back-row players through special replacement procedures. The role cannot serve or block, and cannot complete an attack when the ball is entirely above the net at contact. Defensive specialization therefore comes with defined playing restrictions.

evidence.locator: 19.3.1, printed p. 42 / PDF p. 44; 19.3.2.1-2, printed p. 43 / PDF p. 45

original_record.label: Libero in volleyball
original_record.learning_takeaway: A back-row specialist has distinct replacement rights and attacking, blocking and serving limits.

relations.note: FIVB Rule 19 defines the Libero’s role, playing actions and replacements within volleyball.

original_record.card: This Luba memory board communicates through incised designs and relief carving, whereas many other lukasa use attached beads and shells. The Met’s interpretation connects its motifs with political history and territory. Senior Mbudye members learned to decipher the board within a specialized knowledge tradition.

evidence.locator: Curatorial description, lines 10–16; Artwork Details, object number 1977.467.3

original_record.label: Lukasa memory board (Met 1977.467.3)
original_record.learning_takeaway: Examine how this carved board supports trained historical interpretation.

original_record.card: In matching-market unraveling, participants arrange appointments progressively earlier to get ahead of competitors. Contracts can be signed before candidates’ qualifications or employers’ needs are clear. Roth and Xing’s historical examples show how this timing race can thin later opportunities.

evidence.locator: Introduction, lines 87-91 and 146-164; I. Unraveling in a prototypical market, lines 177-197

original_record.label: Unraveling in matching markets
original_record.learning_takeaway: Competition to secure matches can push offers earlier, before useful information becomes available.

relations.note: Editorial bridge to stable matching: the authors distinguish appointment-date instability from blocking-pair instability and discuss centralized match procedures.

original_record.card: In Maximum Score golf, the committee sets a cap on the score for each hole. A player who does not finish the hole still receives that capped score. The format remains stroke play while bounding the contribution of a difficult hole.
original_record.label: Maximum Score golf
original_record.learning_takeaway: A committee-set cap limits each hole’s stroke score, including holes not finished.

relations.note: Capped stroke totals differ from Stableford points and scoring in sport generally.

original_record.card: Mbudye is a Luba association charged with preserving and interpreting political and historical principles. Its councils could check or reinforce chiefly power. Members progressed through levels of knowledge, with those at the highest level authorized to interpret the intricate designs of lukasa memory boards.

evidence.locator: Curatorial description, lines 12–14

original_record.label: Mbudye association
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect specialized historical knowledge with checks on chiefly power.

relations.note: Editorial placement based on the association’s documented Luba state role.

original_record.card: The McGurk effect occurs when conflicting heard and seen speech can produce a perceived syllable present in neither input. Auditory ba paired with visual ga can be heard as da. Responses vary across listeners and stimuli, showing variability in audiovisual speech integration.

evidence.locator: Abstract and Introduction, PDF pp. 1-2, lines 8-28 and 63-80

original_record.label: McGurk effect
original_record.learning_takeaway: Mismatched heard and seen syllables can produce a perceived syllable present in neither input.

relations.note: The paper characterizes a perceptual speech illusion; perception is a general editorial parent.

original_record.card: Membership closure occurs when someone joins an activity or organization through a friend’s existing affiliation. The added edge connects person and focus. In a social-affiliation network, existing friendships can therefore help shape new memberships.

evidence.locator: 4.3, Co-Evolution of Social and Affiliation Networks, PDF pp. 12-13, lines 375-402

original_record.label: Membership closure
original_record.learning_takeaway: An existing friendship can lead to a new affiliation.

relations.note: Friendship can create a person-to-focus membership edge.

original_record.card: A Merkle consistency proof connects an earlier tree root to a larger tree root through intermediate hashes. It establishes that the earlier leaves remain an unchanged prefix, supporting append-only history. This checks continuity between trees rather than one leaf’s membership.
original_record.label: Merkle consistency proof
original_record.learning_takeaway: Intermediate hashes establish that a larger tree preserves an earlier tree’s unchanged prefix.

relations.note: Append-only prefix preservation differs from leaf membership and general cryptography.

original_record.card: A Merkle inclusion proof supplies the sibling hashes needed to recompute a tree’s root from one leaf. Matching an authenticated root establishes that leaf’s membership under the hash assumptions. It proves inclusion, rather than preservation of the entire earlier tree.
original_record.label: Merkle inclusion proof
original_record.learning_takeaway: An authentication path recomputes a root to establish one leaf’s membership in a tree.

relations.note: One-leaf membership differs from append-only consistency; cryptography is the broad parent.

original_record.card: Metaphysical grounding asks what makes a fact hold in virtue of another, rather than what caused it earlier. Philosophers use picketing as constituting a strike to illustrate the distinction. The disputed notion concerns constitutive explanation or determination, not just a necessary connection.

evidence.locator: Introduction, lines 13–18; §1.1 Determination and explanation

original_record.label: Metaphysical grounding
original_record.learning_takeaway: Separate constitutive dependence from causal history.

relations.note: The entry explicitly locates grounding questions within metaphysics.

original_record.card: Moral hazard in teams arises when individual actions are hidden but joint output is observable. In Holmström’s model, sharing that output under a balanced budget can leave members with incentives to free ride. The team setting changes the contract-design problem.

evidence.locator: Abstract and Introduction, printed pp.324-325 / PDF pp.2-3; free-rider discussion, printed p.325 / PDF p.3

original_record.label: Moral hazard in teams
original_record.learning_takeaway: Shared observable output with hidden individual actions creates a team-specific free-riding problem.

relations.note: The introduction explicitly defines the paper’s setting as a multiagent extension of the moral-hazard problem.

original_record.card: A multitask incentive model treats effort as attention allocated across different duties. When duties compete for that attention, rewarding easily measured output can divert effort from valuable work that is harder to measure. The effect depends on task substitution and measurement.

evidence.locator: Introduction, printed pp. 24-26 / PDF pages 1-2, distinguishing mark and competing-attention paragraphs

original_record.label: Multitask incentive problem
original_record.learning_takeaway: Rewarding measurable output can shift effort away from other valuable duties competing for attention.

relations.note: The introduction explicitly contrasts multidimensional principal-agent models with one-dimensional models.

original_record.card: Muon tomography uses scattering of naturally occurring cosmic-ray muons to reconstruct three-dimensional images of hidden material. Tracking changes in particle paths provides the information without adding an artificial radiation dose. Long exposures, limited position resolution and complex reconstruction remain practical challenges.

evidence.locator: Abstract; lines 15-17
evidence.note: Coulomb scattering enables natural-flux imaging with stated limitations.

original_record.label: Muon tomography
original_record.learning_takeaway: Natural muon scattering can reveal dense hidden structures without an added artificial radiation source.

relations.note: Source explicitly uses muon paths and scattering for imaging.

original_record.card: Mutual exclusivity is a word-learning default that discourages assigning an unfamiliar label to an already named whole object. It can guide a learner toward an unnamed object or property. Context can override the assumption; objects may legitimately have multiple names.

evidence.locator: Mutual Exclusivity, printed pp. 140-141 / PDF pp. 4-5; Constraints as Default Assumptions, pp. 142-145

original_record.label: Mutual exclusivity in word learning
original_record.learning_takeaway: An unfamiliar label can be assigned to an unnamed object or property instead of a familiar whole object.

relations.note: The authors explicitly treat mutual exclusivity as a proposed constraint guiding children’s acquisition of word meanings.

original_record.card: Nafion is a named family of fluorinated polymer membranes used in electrochemical applications. Its sulfonic membranes are based on a perfluorosulfonic-acid and PTFE copolymer and conduct positively charged ions. The membrane's polymer composition is tied to its role inside electrochemical cells.

evidence.locator: Membranes for a Wide Variety of Electrochemical Applications; lines 151-153; grades tables
evidence.note: Manufacturer identifies copolymer basis and cation conduction.

original_record.label: Nafion
original_record.learning_takeaway: A named fluorinated polymer membrane family conducts cations in electrochemical cells.

relations.note: Manufacturer explicitly identifies a polymer membrane family.

original_record.card: Natural Earth is a compromise world-map projection with rounded corners. It preserves neither areas nor angles exactly. High-latitude regions appear enlarged, while angular distortion increases toward the edges, showing why an attractive general-purpose map still requires care when comparing regions.

evidence.locator: Description; Distortion; Limitations

original_record.label: Natural Earth projection
original_record.learning_takeaway: Recognize distortion within a rounded world-map compromise.

relations.note: Esri identifies Natural Earth as a world-map projection.

original_record.card: Negative pressure wound therapy uses a sealed dressing connected to a suction pump. Removing wound fluid and reducing swelling can support healing. Clinicians select suitable wounds for this treatment; the intended outcome does not make the device appropriate for every wound.

evidence.locator: Definition and mechanism; lines 50-76; indications and contraindications, lines 78-104
evidence.note: Sealed-dressing suction removes fluid and reduces swelling.

original_record.label: Negative pressure wound therapy
original_record.learning_takeaway: Controlled suction removes wound fluid while a sealed dressing supports healing.

relations.note: Provider-directed treatment supports editorial placement under medicine.
Source identifies wound healing as the intended outcome.

original_record.card: Published between 1936 and 1966, with a wartime interruption, the Green Book listed businesses welcoming African American travelers. Reports from readers and postal-worker contacts helped build its directory. Hotels, restaurants, and service stations turned shared local knowledge into a practical response to segregation.

evidence.locator: Publication and directory history, lines 24–35

original_record.label: The Negro Motorist Green Book
original_record.learning_takeaway: Trace how shared information supported travel under segregation.

relations.note: Editorial historical placement based on the documented segregation context.

original_record.card: Nembutsu is a Buddhist chanting practice. At the Buddhist Temple of Marin, a Jodo Shinshu community, chanting Namo Amida Butsu expresses gratitude. The temple places this chant alongside listening and compassionate living, illustrating a devotional function within one specific Buddhist tradition.

evidence.locator: Tradition statement and practices, lines 118, 145–165

original_record.label: Nembutsu
original_record.learning_takeaway: Recognize gratitude as the chant’s described devotional function.

relations.note: The temple identifies Nembutsu within its Buddhist practices.

original_record.card: NIST SRM 610 is a trace-element glass reference material. A piece aboard NASA's Perseverance rover helps calibrate PIXL, an instrument that measures elements in Martian rocks. A characterized Earth material supplies a reference for interpreting measurements made on another planet.

evidence.locator: PIXL calibration discussion; lines 126-130
evidence.note: Glass reference material calibrates Perseverance's PIXL.

original_record.label: NIST SRM 610
original_record.learning_takeaway: Characterized trace-element glass can calibrate elemental measurements on Mars.

relations.note: Calibration premises support an editorial metrology application.
Source explicitly identifies SRM 610 as glass.

original_record.card: Nixtamalization cooks and steeps maize in an alkaline solution, commonly containing food-grade lime (calcium hydroxide). Washing and milling turn the kernels into dough for foods such as tortillas. Lime cooking increases calcium content; processing also makes niacin more available.

evidence.locator: What is nixtamalization?, lines 26–29; chemical changes and nutrition, lines 34–42
evidence.note: Alkaline processing produces dough; lime cooking increases calcium, and processing improves niacin availability.

original_record.label: Nixtamalization
original_record.learning_takeaway: Alkaline maize processing changes dough preparation and nutrient availability.

relations.note: Cooking, soaking and milling support editorial food-processing placement.
Source explicitly names maize as the processed material.

original_record.card: Non-refoulement protects people against return to prohibited danger. UNHCR’s account explains that refugee protection can apply before formal status recognition: returning an applicant prematurely could defeat it. Applicable dangers and exceptions depend on the governing refugee or human rights instrument.

evidence.locator: Legal basis, Beneficiaries and Exceptions, lines 44–79, 107–120

original_record.label: Non-refoulement
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect protection before recognition with instrument-specific rules.

relations.note: The note locates non-refoulement in international refugee law.

original_record.card: A nonunion is a broken bone that fails to heal, rather than a fracture that is merely healing slowly. Bone repair depends on stability, blood supply and nutrition. The distinction requires clinical and imaging context; it is not defined by one universal waiting period.

evidence.locator: Definition and bone healing; lines 118-123; diagnosis; lines 174-178
evidence.note: Failure differs from delay; stability and blood supply support healing.

original_record.label: Nonunion
original_record.learning_takeaway: A fracture that fails to heal differs from one that is merely healing slowly.

relations.note: Source explicitly defines failure of a fracture to heal.

original_record.card: Oblivious HTTP sends encrypted requests through a relay to a gateway. The relay sees the client but cannot read the request; the gateway decrypts it but sees the relay. Privacy depends on separated knowledge, including those parties not colluding.

evidence.locator: 2.1 Applicability; section 6, lines 540-550

original_record.label: Oblivious HTTP
original_record.learning_takeaway: Separate relay and gateway split knowledge of client identity and request contents.

relations.note: RFC 9458 defines an encrypted relaying mechanism for HTTP requests and responses, a distinct protocol facet.

original_record.card: Occultation for weed control uses an opaque cover to block light over a garden bed. Warmth and moisture can encourage seeds to sprout, while darkness prevents the seedlings from sustaining growth. Weather and site conditions affect how the process performs.

evidence.locator: Clear versus opaque coverings; Quick facts and methods; lines 244-270, 287-299
evidence.note: Opaque covers combine germination conditions with light exclusion.

original_record.label: Occultation for weed control
original_record.learning_takeaway: Opaque covers block light while moisture and warmth exhaust newly sprouted weeds.

relations.note: Guide explicitly uses occultation for garden-bed weed control.

original_record.card: Ottava rima organizes a stanza into eight lines rhyming abababcc, usually in iambic pentameter. After six lines alternate two rhymes, the closing couplet introduces a paired ending. The form can carry longer poems, including Byron’s Don Juan.

evidence.locator: “About Form”; CLERIHEW; DOUBLE-DACTYL; OTTAVA RIMA; SPENSERIAN STANZA

original_record.label: Ottava rima
original_record.learning_takeaway: Follow alternating rhymes into a closing couplet.

relations.note: The Poetry Archive explicitly identifies ottava rima as a stanza form.

original_record.card: P-factor is asymmetric propeller loading at a high angle of attack. The blades experience unequal relative airflow, shifting the effective center of thrust away from the shaft. This creates a yawing tendency whose direction depends on propeller rotation.

evidence.locator: Chapter 5, Asymmetric Loading (P-Factor), printed p. 5-32 / PDF p. 32

original_record.label: P-factor
original_record.learning_takeaway: High angle of attack gives propeller blades unequal loading and shifts thrust away from the shaft center.

relations.note: The passage explains the mechanism through the rotating propeller blades and displacement of the thrust center.

original_record.card: Pacta sunt servanda requires parties to perform treaties in force in good faith. Article 26 of the Vienna Convention joins two obligations: a treaty binds its parties, and those parties must carry it out.

evidence.locator: Article 26, printed page 10

original_record.label: Pacta sunt servanda
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect binding force with performance.

relations.note: The rule governs treaty performance.

original_record.card: This late-thirteenth-century Yuan safe-conduct pass carries an imperial inscription in Phakpa script. Silver fills an openwork design so its characters project on both sides, reversed on the back. The artifact connects official authority with the material construction and visibility of its written command.

evidence.locator: Curatorial description, lines 7–11; Artwork Details, object 1993.256

original_record.label: Safe Conduct Pass in Phakpa script (Met 1993.256)
original_record.learning_takeaway: Read imperial authority through an inscription’s material construction.

relations.note: Editorial Yuan-dynasty placement based on the museum’s object attribution.

original_record.card: Pansori is a Korean narrative vocal genre performed by one singer and one drummer. The singer develops an epic story through poetic, dramatic and musical expression. Sugungga illustrates how this small performing partnership can carry an extended tale with multiple characters.

evidence.locator: Program pamphlet text, lines 100–105

original_record.label: Pansori
original_record.learning_takeaway: Trace narrative performance through singer and drummer.

relations.note: The program identifies pansori as a Korean vocal genre.

original_record.card: Peirce quincuncial places the world inside a square that can tile a larger surface. It preserves local angles except at the middle of each edge, where areas become strongly exaggerated. A seamless-looking mosaic therefore does not imply uniformly low distortion.

evidence.locator: Description; Graticule; Distortion; Usage

original_record.label: Peirce quincuncial projection
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish map tiling from uniform distortion control.

relations.note: Esri identifies Peirce quincuncial as a map projection.

original_record.card: Photobleaching irreversibly removes a fluorescent molecule's ability to emit light through photochemical destruction during illumination. A fading image can therefore reflect damage to the fluorescent label rather than disappearance of the structure being observed. Not every loss of fluorescence is photobleaching.

evidence.locator: Fading, Quenching, and Photobleaching; lines 88-95
evidence.note: Irreversible fluorophore destruction is distinguished from broader fading.

original_record.label: Photobleaching
original_record.learning_takeaway: Repeated illumination can irreversibly remove a molecule's fluorescence.

relations.note: Source explains a mechanism of fluorescence loss.

original_record.card: A polymer's properties can change through structural recovery, a process called physical aging. This affects viscoelastic behavior and engineering properties. Understanding a polymer glass therefore involves more than locating its glass transition: its recovering structure also matters.

evidence.locator: Abstract; lines 125-127
evidence.note: Structural recovery affects polymer mechanical properties.

original_record.label: Physical aging of polymers
original_record.learning_takeaway: Structural recovery changes a polymer's viscoelastic properties over time.

relations.note: Abstract explicitly associates physical aging with polymer properties.

original_record.card: Pinpeat is Cambodia’s court music tradition. Smithsonian’s diaspora lesson asks how Cambodian American artists sustain and transform it in the United States. Studying both settings shows how cultural preservation can include adaptation as musicians encounter new social contexts.

evidence.locator: Lesson introduction and learning objectives, lines 440–455

original_record.label: Pinpeat
original_record.learning_takeaway: Compare preservation and adaptation across community settings.

relations.note: The lesson identifies pinpeat as Cambodian court music.

original_record.card: After the 1944 Port Chicago explosion, 258 Black sailors refused renewed ammunition-loading work; fifty were convicted of mutiny. Their case exposed the intersection of dangerous work and racial discrimination in the Navy. The Secretary of the Navy exonerated the sailors on July 17, 2024.

evidence.locator: The Aftermath and Mutiny; Trial Proceedings; Exoneration, lines 39–47 and 55

original_record.label: Port Chicago mutiny trial
original_record.learning_takeaway: Compare an unjust wartime conviction with later exoneration.

relations.note: Editorial placement based on documented segregation in the US Navy.

original_record.card: Preferential attachment is a rule in which well-connected nodes are more likely to receive new links. Repeated growth can amplify an initial advantage, producing a few highly connected nodes. This is a simplified network model, not a universal explanation of popularity.

evidence.locator: 18.3 Rich-Get-Richer Models, PDF pp. 5-6, lines 122-156 and 168-171

original_record.label: Preferential attachment
original_record.learning_takeaway: A node’s existing links can increase its chance of receiving new links, amplifying early differences.

relations.note: The source provides a network-growth model of link creation; network science is an editorial parent.

original_record.card: In Kapur’s 2006 study, student groups initially struggled with ill-structured problems without scaffolding. They later performed better on individual problems, including transfer, than a scaffolded comparison group. The result concerns that staged task design; unsuccessful exploration alone is not a general recipe.

evidence.locator: Abstract, PDF p. 1, lines 4-22; Method/Research Design, printed p. 1588 / PDF p. 2, lines 148-195

original_record.label: Productive failure
original_record.learning_takeaway: Unsuccessful problem exploration can support later transfer when subsequent problems supply a useful contrast.

relations.note: The experiment explicitly analyzes meaningful learning and transfer after contrasting problem-solving conditions.

original_record.card: A pycnocline is an ocean layer where density increases rapidly with depth. This stable density gradient can restrict exchange between surface and deeper water. Temperature, salinity or both may contribute, so a density boundary need not match one single temperature or salt boundary.

evidence.locator: Main pycnocline and salinity layers; PDF page 2 (zero-based 1), lines 145-179
evidence.note: Strong density gradient separates ocean layers and limits mixing.

original_record.label: Pycnocline
original_record.learning_takeaway: A steep increase of density with depth can limit mixing between ocean layers.

relations.note: Source explicitly identifies a density-stratified ocean zone.

original_record.card: QPACK compresses HTTP/3 field sections using a shared dynamic table and separate instruction streams. Referring to a table entry that has not arrived can block decoding. Limiting blocked streams trades compression reuse against the cost of waiting.

evidence.locator: Sections 1, 2, 2.1.2

original_record.label: QPACK field compression
original_record.learning_takeaway: Separate instruction streams let HTTP/3 field compression trade table reuse against blocked decoding.

relations.note: RFC 9204 defines QPACK for HTTP/3 field compression, a specific mechanism within HTTP.

original_record.card: Odilon Redon’s 1895 lithograph The Buddha appeared in the ninth L’Estampe Originale album. Printed using chine collé, it combines black ink with light gray paper. The Met’s account shows how the paper itself contributes the image’s cool background tone.

evidence.locator: Print identification and curatorial explanation, lines 42–45

original_record.label: The Buddha (Odilon Redon lithograph, 1895)
original_record.learning_takeaway: Identify paper color’s contribution to this lithograph.

relations.note: The Buddha is identified in the portfolio’s ninth album.

original_record.card: After malnutrition, restarting nutrition can trigger dangerous electrolyte shifts as carbohydrate metabolism resumes. Cells draw phosphorus, potassium and magnesium from the blood, potentially leaving blood levels too low. Refeeding syndrome shows why nutritional recovery can require clinical monitoring as well as renewed food intake.

evidence.locator: Definition and electrolyte mechanism; lines 53, 69-79; clinical monitoring, lines 150-159
evidence.note: Renewed metabolism shifts electrolytes into cells after malnutrition.

original_record.label: Refeeding syndrome
original_record.learning_takeaway: Restarting nutrition after malnutrition can produce dangerous electrolyte shifts.

relations.note: Source explicitly describes a complication following malnutrition.

original_record.card: Relative performance evaluation lets a contract use peers’ outcomes alongside an agent’s own performance. In Holmström’s model, comparing agents can provide information useful for incentives. The value of competition therefore depends on its informational role in the contracting problem.

evidence.locator: Abstract and Introduction, printed pp.324-325 / PDF pp.2-3; relative-performance evaluation paragraph, printed p.325 / PDF p.3

original_record.label: Relative performance evaluation
original_record.learning_takeaway: Peers’ outcomes can supply information useful for designing an individual’s incentive contract.

relations.note: The abstract and introduction explain how peers’ outcomes inform incentive contracts in the model.

original_record.card: A root hair is a slender extension of a root epidermal cell, with its wall and membrane projecting into the surrounding growing medium. Water and nutrients enter through these fine outgrowths, connecting the root's surface to its supply.

evidence.locator: Dermal tissue; lines 224-226
evidence.note: Root epidermal outgrowths absorb water and nutrients.

original_record.label: Root hair
original_record.learning_takeaway: A fine epidermal-cell outgrowth provides an entry route for water and nutrients.

relations.note: Passage identifies hairs in root dermal tissue.

original_record.card: Rugby union advantage allows play to continue after an infringement when the non-offending team gains clear tactical or territorial benefit. A mere opportunity is insufficient. Subject to the law’s exceptions, the referee can return to the original infringement when no advantage materializes.

evidence.locator: Principle and 7.1-7.3, lines 38-59

original_record.label: Advantage in rugby union
original_record.learning_takeaway: Play can continue after infringement when the opponents gain clear tactical or territorial advantage.

relations.note: World Rugby expressly makes advantage a law governing rugby play.

original_record.card: A runway incursion is an incorrect presence of an aircraft, vehicle or person in the protected area of a surface designated for aircraft landing and takeoff. The FAA safety category describes an occurrence, including cases without immediate collision consequences.

evidence.locator: Definition and Category D, lines 115-125

original_record.label: Runway incursion
original_record.learning_takeaway: Incorrect presence on a runway protected area qualifies even without immediate collision consequences.

relations.note: Runway is infrastructure; an incursion is a separately defined safety occurrence.

original_record.card: With fixed quotas, strict preferences and responsive hospital rankings, stable hospital–doctor matchings fill the same number of places at each hospital. The rural hospitals theorem also fixes which doctors an undersubscribed hospital receives, even when other assignments change.

evidence.locator: Section 3 fixed responsive hospital quotas, PDF p.7, lines 117-141; section 4 rural hospitals theorem, PDF p.8, lines 143-159

original_record.label: Rural hospitals theorem
original_record.learning_takeaway: Stable matchings cannot change which doctors an undersubscribed hospital hires under strict responsive preferences.

relations.note: Editorial comparison: this theorem concerns a many-to-one extension of the pinned one-to-one stable matching problem; Q620702 is not a taxonomy parent.

original_record.card: Sanké Môn is an annual collective fishing ritual in San, Mali, commemorating the town’s foundation. Songs, dances, and other practices connect the gathering with local memory and belief. Protecting the Sanké pond preserves both an ecological resource and the setting that sustains the ritual.

evidence.locator: Main French text, lines 24–26 and 34–35

original_record.label: Sanké Môn
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect a collective ritual with its environmental setting.

relations.note: UNESCO explicitly identifies Sanké Môn as a collective ritual.

original_record.card: Saturation flow rate describes the hourly rate at which a queued lane could discharge under continuous green with no lost time. It is a reference flow: an actual signal cycle allocates only some of its time to effective green.
original_record.label: Saturation flow rate at a signalized intersection
original_record.learning_takeaway: Continuous-green discharge with no lost time is a reference rate, distinct from actual signal capacity.

relations.note: Traffic light is a device; saturation flow is a defined discharge-rate quantity.

original_record.card: In Schelling’s simplified two-group models, people move when local neighbors fail their tolerance threshold. Each move changes nearby composition, potentially prompting further moves and producing clusters. The result illustrates a collective pattern without treating real segregation as a single-cause process.
original_record.label: Schelling segregation model
original_record.learning_takeaway: Local neighbor preferences in a simplified movement model can create large segregated regions.

relations.note: Schelling explicitly models segregation by color.

original_record.card: Seam allowance is the fabric area between a stitching line and the raw edge. A seam thus has distinct boundaries: where the pieces are joined and where they were cut. The intervening fabric belongs to the construction allowance, not the stitched line itself.

evidence.locator: Seam Allowance; PDF page 10 (zero-based 9), lines 224-226
evidence.note: Glossary defines area between stitching and raw edge.

original_record.label: Seam allowance
original_record.learning_takeaway: The fabric area between stitching and the raw edge is a separately planned construction allowance.

relations.note: Sewing glossary explicitly defines the construction allowance.

original_record.card: A selvage is the firmly woven edge running lengthwise along woven fabric. It can shrink more than the cloth's main area and pucker a seam, so its construction behavior deserves separate attention.

evidence.locator: Wearing versus design ease; fabric edges; lines 84, 154, 178
evidence.note: Firm lengthwise edges may shrink and pucker seams.

original_record.label: Selvage
original_record.learning_takeaway: A firmly woven fabric edge can behave differently from the cloth body in a seam.

relations.note: Woven-edge premises support editorial placement under cloth.

original_record.card: Sentinel lymph node biopsy identifies and samples the first node or nodes most likely to receive cancer spreading from a tumor. Examining them helps stage the cancer. A negative result suggests no spread to nearby nodes, but cannot guarantee it.

evidence.locator: Definition and procedure; lines 27-40; staging benefit, line 47; false-negative risk, line 59
evidence.note: Selected first nodes are removed and examined for cancer spread.

original_record.label: Sentinel lymph node biopsy
original_record.learning_takeaway: Sampling the first draining lymph node helps investigate whether cancer has spread.

relations.note: Source explicitly describes a biopsy of selected lymph nodes.

original_record.card: Shibori is shaped resist dyeing: fabric is folded, gathered, bound or clamped into three dimensional forms before coloring. When the cloth is flattened, its pattern records both the shape and the pressure that restricted dye access. Structure becomes visible as surface design.

evidence.locator: Definition, lines 128–131

original_record.label: Shibori
original_record.learning_takeaway: Relate three dimensional shaping to the resulting dye pattern.

relations.note: The practitioner network defines shibori as shaped resist dyeing.

original_record.card: Shikantaza is the just sitting approach associated with Japanese Soto Zen. In this account, sitting properly in zazen is itself the right state of mind, rather than merely preparation for later enlightenment. The posture expresses realization within the tradition’s understanding.

evidence.locator: Definition, line 56

original_record.label: Shikantaza
original_record.learning_takeaway: Understand sitting as realization within Soto practice.

relations.note: The definition presents shikantaza as an approach within zazen.

original_record.card: In a Simon task, a stimulus’s color or shape determines the required response while its location is irrelevant. Responses are often faster when stimulus and response occur on corresponding sides. The Simon effect shows that irrelevant spatial information can influence action selection.

evidence.locator: Instruction, lines 139-146

original_record.label: Simon effect
original_record.learning_takeaway: An irrelevant stimulus location can interfere with a response selected by color or shape.

relations.note: The paper’s experimental response-selection results provide an editorial navigation parent in cognitive psychology.

original_record.card: Soil solarization covers soil with clear plastic to trap solar heat, suppressing weeds and some soil pests. Its effectiveness depends on sunlight, moisture and local conditions. The clear cover's heating mechanism differs from the light exclusion used by opaque covers.

evidence.locator: Clear versus opaque coverings; Quick facts and methods; lines 244-270, 287-299
evidence.note: Clear covers trap heat; results depend on conditions.

original_record.label: Soil solarization
original_record.learning_takeaway: Clear plastic traps solar heat to suppress weeds and some soil pests.

relations.note: Guide explicitly uses solarization to prepare garden beds.
