evidence.locator: Introduction and braking-curve prediction description, lines 15-21

concepts.label: ETCS braking curve
concepts.learning_takeaway: A train-and-track model predicts speed against distance so ETCS can supervise braking toward a limit.

relations.note: The source explicitly describes braking-curve computation as part of ETCS speed-and-position supervision.

concepts.card: Euclidean buffering draws a distance zone using straight-line measurements on a flat coordinate plane. It works best around features concentrated within a suitably projected small region. Where the projection distorts distance substantially, equal map offsets no longer represent equal distances on Earth.

evidence.locator: “Euclidean and geodesic buffering”, method bullets and shape-preserving Geodesic option

concepts.label: Euclidean buffering
concepts.learning_takeaway: Identify when flat-map distance zones inherit projection distortion.

relations.note: Esri names Euclidean buffering as a geographic buffer construction method.

concepts.card: Event Segmentation Theory proposes that people use ongoing models to predict what happens next. A temporary rise in prediction error signals an event boundary and updates processing. The account connects perceived divisions in continuous activity with attention and memory.

evidence.locator: Abstract; A Theory of Event Segmentation, lines 94-113

concepts.label: Event Segmentation Theory
concepts.learning_takeaway: Transient prediction errors mark perceived event boundaries in the proposed account of ongoing activity.

relations.note: The authors explicitly frame the theory as an account of perceptual boundaries in continuous activity.

concepts.card: Ferrar Glacier carries ice from Taylor Dome toward Antarctica's Ross Sea. Snow accumulating at the dome compresses into ice, some of which flows through this glacier and the Royal Society Range. The named route connects inland accumulation with ice reaching the coast.

evidence.locator: Snow accumulation and ice route; lines 268-270
evidence.note: Taylor Dome accumulation supplies the named glacier's seaward route.

concepts.label: Ferrar Glacier
concepts.learning_takeaway: A named glacier connects inland snow accumulation with an ice-flow route toward the sea.

relations.note: NASA explicitly describes Ferrar as a river of ice.

concepts.card: Fitting-attitude theories explain value through responses that an object merits. Being admirable, for example, is explained through the fittingness of admiration. The claim concerns appropriate responses, not whatever people happen to feel, so actual affection or dislike alone does not settle an object’s value.

evidence.locator: Introduction, lines 13–20

concepts.label: Fitting-attitude theories of value
concepts.learning_takeaway: Distinguish a deserved response from an actual feeling.

relations.note: The entry explicitly presents these as theories explaining value.

concepts.card: Focal closure occurs when two people sharing an activity or organization form a social tie. The shared focus supplies a setting for contact. In a social-affiliation network, the resulting edge connects people.

evidence.locator: 4.3, Co-Evolution of Social and Affiliation Networks, PDF p. 12, lines 370-374

concepts.label: Focal closure
concepts.learning_takeaway: A shared activity can help create a friendship.

relations.note: Shared affiliations can create a social tie.

concepts.card: The friendship paradox reflects sampling through social ties. People with many friends appear in more people’s friend lists, so they are overrepresented among friends. Average friend counts can consequently be higher in this sample; the statement concerns sampling rather than every individual.

evidence.locator: Abstract, lines 46-48

concepts.label: Friendship paradox
concepts.learning_takeaway: Sampling people through friendship links overrepresents people who have many friends.

relations.note: The original abstract explicitly explains comparisons of friend counts in a social network through disproportionate exposure to highly connected friends.

concepts.card: Frost heave raises ground as ice grows within freezing soil, sometimes deforming road surfaces. Growing ice layers can draw in additional water that freezes, enlarging the layer. The movement therefore need not result solely from expansion of water already occupying soil pores.

evidence.locator: Density of frozen water and cryosuction; lines 89-94
evidence.note: Ice growth and additional water can heave frozen ground.

concepts.label: Frost heave
concepts.learning_takeaway: Growing ice in soil can raise the ground and deform a road surface.

relations.note: Soil-water and ice-growth premises support editorial soil-physics placement.

concepts.card: Gamelan gong kebyar is a Balinese ensemble style that emerged in northern Bali around 1915. Rapid tempo changes and dynamic interlocking parts distinguish its repertoire. An album labeled court music illustrates a contextual trap: most documented performances belonged to other settings.

evidence.locator: David Harnish’s guest article, lines 450–468

concepts.label: Gamelan gong kebyar
concepts.learning_takeaway: Hear musical dynamics while checking performance context.

relations.note: Gong kebyar is identified as a gamelan style.

concepts.card: Gathering draws a longer length of fabric into small folds so it fits a shorter attaching edge. In a machine-sewn ruffle, long stitches provide threads that can be pulled and adjusted. Distributing the folds lets the ruffle fit its band.

evidence.locator: Gathering stitches and ruffle attachment; lines 317-336
evidence.note: Pulled gathering threads fit a ruffle to its band.

concepts.label: Gathering in sewing
concepts.learning_takeaway: Draw longer cloth into small folds so it fits a shorter attaching edge.

relations.note: Source explicitly gathers a ruffle in a sewing project.

concepts.card: Generating a word from a cue can leave a stronger memory than reading it. The generation effect emerged in experiments comparing those encoding conditions, with advantages in later recognition and recall. Its size and occurrence depend on the study conditions.

evidence.locator: Original abstract summary and author retrospective, single PDF page, lines 3-8 and 26-43

concepts.label: Generation effect
concepts.learning_takeaway: Generating a word can improve later memory compared with reading the same word.

relations.note: The author describes the original experiments as comparisons of memory for generated and read words.

concepts.card: Geodesic buffering builds distance zones while accounting for Earth’s curved spheroidal surface. It is useful over large extents and near poles or the date line. A zone may look distorted on a flat map while showing the intended distance correctly on a globe.

evidence.locator: “Euclidean and geodesic buffering”, method bullets and shape-preserving Geodesic option

concepts.label: Geodesic buffering
concepts.learning_takeaway: Separate curved-surface distance from flat-map appearance.

relations.note: Esri names geodesic buffering as a geographic buffer construction method.

concepts.card: In an amorphous polymer, the glass transition marks a temperature range where chain segments gain substantial mobility. The material changes from glassy behavior toward rubbery behavior. This differs from melting crystalline regions: segment movement and crystalline order describe different changes.

evidence.locator: Long-range segmental motion; Glass Transition vs. Melting; lines 25-26 and 51-56
evidence.note: Segmental mobility changes; crystalline melting is distinguished.

concepts.label: Glass transition
concepts.learning_takeaway: Amorphous polymer segment motion changes across a temperature range, separately from crystalline melting.

relations.note: Source explicitly explains a polymer transition.

concepts.card: GN-z11 is a distant galaxy seen about 430 million years after the Big Bang. NASA's 2024 Webb report describes extended host-galaxy light and a compact central source. Its colors and gas signatures support a black-hole interpretation, illustrating how indirect observations investigate early galaxies.

evidence.locator: Host galaxy and compact source; lines 322-336
evidence.note: Dated report resolves host and compact source with black-hole evidence.

concepts.label: GN-z11
concepts.learning_takeaway: Resolve host-galaxy light from a compact source to investigate an early galaxy's unusual brightness.

relations.note: NASA explicitly identifies GN-z11 and its host component as a galaxy.

concepts.card: For a spherical Earth, Goode homolosine combines sinusoidal and Mollweide projections to preserve areas. Its familiar interrupted versions split the map into lobes emphasizing land or oceans. These cuts reduce the shape distortion found near the edges of its uninterrupted form.

evidence.locator: Description; Graticule; Usage; Limitations

concepts.label: Goode homolosine projection
concepts.learning_takeaway: Understand how interruptions trade continuity for reduced shape distortion.

relations.note: Esri identifies Goode homolosine as a map projection.

concepts.card: Grainline in woven fabric follows its threads, whose lengthwise and crosswise directions should meet at right angles. A printed stripe can be off grain. Aligning pieces by the print alone may therefore produce difficulties when matching patterns or cutting straight pieces.

evidence.locator: Checking fabric grain and printing; lines 69-73
evidence.note: Thread grain differs from printed design alignment.

concepts.label: Grainline in woven fabric
concepts.learning_takeaway: Thread direction, rather than a printed stripe, determines whether fabric is on grain.

relations.note: Cutting-alignment premises support an editorial sewing facet.

concepts.card: Guard cells occur in pairs around a stoma, an opening in a plant's surface. By opening that pore, they let gases pass between the surrounding air and deeper leaf cells. The cells and the opening are distinct structures.

evidence.locator: Dermal tissue; lines 224-226
evidence.note: Paired cells open stomata for gas exchange.

concepts.label: Guard cell
concepts.learning_takeaway: Paired guard cells control an opening used for leaf gas exchange.

relations.note: Passage locates guard cells around stomata.

concepts.card: Gyotaku transfers a fish’s surface to paper by rubbing it over an inked specimen. The print records details of shape and texture. In a Smithsonian educational version, rubber replicas replace real fish; excessive paint blurs the transfer, making material quantity part of the result.

evidence.locator: Catherine Sutera’s museum account, lines 65–69

concepts.label: Gyotaku
concepts.learning_takeaway: Connect transferred detail with paint quantity and surface contact.

relations.note: Documented ink and paper transfer supports this printmaking placement.

concepts.card: Haibun combines prose and haiku, a literary form originating in Japan. The prose often describes an environment and precedes a poem whose connection remains implicit. In Bashō’s travel writing, the surrounding narrative and individual haiku create meaning together without spelling out every link.

evidence.locator: Definition; “From A Poet’s Glossary”, prose–haiku relationship

concepts.label: Haibun
concepts.learning_takeaway: Read prose and haiku through their implicit connection.

relations.note: The Academy identifies haibun as a literary poetic form.

concepts.card: A halocline is a layer where salinity changes rapidly with depth. Fresher surface water over saltier water can create one. It describes a salt gradient, while a pycnocline describes density and a thermocline describes temperature; these layers need not coincide.

evidence.locator: Main pycnocline and salinity layers; PDF page 2 (zero-based 1), lines 145-179
evidence.note: Ocean salinity-gradient layer distinguished from density and temperature layers.

concepts.label: Halocline
concepts.learning_takeaway: A salinity gradient can separate fresher surface water from saltier deep water.

relations.note: Source explicitly describes a salinity-stratified ocean zone.

concepts.card: A single plane can simultaneously divide each of three finite-volume solids in three-dimensional space into equal volumes. The ham sandwich theorem extends this pattern: in n dimensions, one hyperplane can bisect n finite volumes, however differently they are positioned.

evidence.locator: Theorem statement and three-dimensional argument; lines 13-20
evidence.note: Simultaneous finite-volume bisection in matching dimension.

concepts.label: Ham sandwich theorem
concepts.learning_takeaway: One plane can simultaneously bisect three three-dimensional volumes.

relations.note: Dimension and continuous-volume premises support editorial topology placement.

concepts.card: The Japanese Hayabusa2 mission collected samples from asteroid Ryugu and returned them to Earth in 2020. Its instruments and small rovers explored the surface. Returning material lets laboratory analysis complement spacecraft observations, giving researchers physical asteroid samples to examine directly.

evidence.locator: Mission overview, sample return and craft design; lines 241, 264, 304-312
evidence.note: Ryugu exploration and completed 2020 sample return.

concepts.label: Hayabusa2
concepts.learning_takeaway: Returning physical asteroid samples lets laboratory analysis complement spacecraft observations.

relations.note: Sampling and return support editorial space-exploration placement.
NASA explicitly names an asteroid as the mission's study target.

concepts.card: A hazard pointer lets a thread announce that it is protecting an object in concurrent memory. Removed objects are retired before reclamation. Checking published hazard pointers delays freeing protected objects, separating removal from safe reuse of their memory.

evidence.locator: 2 Hazard pointer overview, PDF pp. 4-5, lines 125-162

concepts.label: Hazard pointer
concepts.learning_takeaway: Reclaim nodes removed from lock-free objects for safe later reuse.

relations.note: Concurrent computing is broader than this named memory-reclamation methodology.

concepts.card: In Fricker’s account, hermeneutical injustice arises when unequal shared interpretive resources leave someone unfairly unable to understand a social experience. Sexual harassment before that concept gained recognition illustrates the problem: the obstacle lies partly in collective understanding, rather than only one listener’s disbelief.

evidence.locator: Printed page 1, hermeneutical-injustice definition and harassment example

concepts.label: Hermeneutical injustice
concepts.learning_takeaway: Locate an interpretive obstacle within unequal shared resources.

relations.note: Fricker explicitly identifies this form of epistemic injustice.

concepts.card: Homophily is the tendency for social ties to connect similar people. Shared traits can shape who meets whom and who forms a friendship. It describes a population pattern, allowing many individual ties between unlike people.

evidence.locator: 4.1 Homophily, PDF pp. 2-3, lines 23-45 and 64-78

concepts.label: Homophily
concepts.learning_takeaway: Shared traits often accompany social ties.

relations.note: Similarity among connected people in social networks.

concepts.card: Hotine oblique Mercator aligns a conformal map with a region extending diagonally rather than north–south or east–west. It preserves angles and shapes locally, but area and distance distortion increase away from the central region. Orientation therefore matters when choosing a regional projection.

evidence.locator: Description; Distortion; Usage; Variants

concepts.label: Hotine oblique Mercator projection
concepts.learning_takeaway: Match a conformal projection to an oblique region.

relations.note: Esri identifies Hotine oblique Mercator as a map projection.

concepts.card: HTTP Message Signatures authenticate selected request or response components and accompanying signature metadata. The signer builds a defined signature base from those covered parts. Verification therefore concerns the named coverage; it does not automatically authenticate every field or every message byte.

evidence.locator: Abstract; section 3, line 1399; 1.1 Terminology; 7.3.3 Symmetric Cryptography, official text companion lines 254-276 and 3267-3287

concepts.label: HTTP Message Signatures
concepts.learning_takeaway: A signature verifies the chosen covered HTTP components and associated signature metadata.

relations.note: The RFC applies digital signatures to HTTP signature bases; its symmetric-MAC option lies outside this digital-signature parent.

concepts.card: An HTTP Structured Fields dictionary is an ordered collection of unique textual keys and typed values. Values may be individual items or inner lists. A field specification gives those keys meaning, letting a common parser handle the representation.

evidence.locator: 3 Structured Data Types, lines 252-259; 3.2 Dictionaries, lines 330-336; 2.4 compatibility, lines 243-246

concepts.label: HTTP structured field dictionary
concepts.learning_takeaway: HTTP field dictionaries map unique textual keys to typed items or inner lists.

relations.note: The specification explicitly defines Dictionaries as a top-level representation for HTTP fields.

concepts.card: Complementarity gives the International Criminal Court a role alongside national criminal justice. Under the inspected Rome Statute, genuine domestic investigation or prosecution can make a case inadmissible. Proceedings that shield a suspect illustrate unwillingness; other jurisdiction and admissibility conditions also apply.

evidence.locator: Preamble, Article 1, Article 17 (lines 18, 25, 244–258)

concepts.label: Complementarity (International Criminal Court)
concepts.learning_takeaway: Evaluate genuine domestic proceedings before ICC admissibility.

relations.note: Articles 1 and 17 establish the ICC’s complementary role.

concepts.card: The Ignatian Examen is Christian prayer through reflection on daily experience. One adapted sequence begins with awareness of God, reviews gratitude and emotions, then prays over one feature of the day and looks toward tomorrow. Ordinary events become material for discernment.

evidence.locator: Main explanation and five-step method, lines 85–98

concepts.label: Ignatian Examen
concepts.learning_takeaway: Use daily events as material for reflective prayer.

relations.note: The source describes an adapted Christian prayer method.

concepts.card: The illusion of explanatory depth occurs when a feeling of understanding exceeds one’s ability to explain a mechanism. Attempting a detailed explanation can expose gaps and lower confidence. In the experiments, this gap was especially apparent for explanatory understanding.

evidence.locator: Abstract and Introduction, PDF pp. 1-2, lines 8-17 and 54-65; discussion of recalibration after explanation, PDF p. 15, lines 482-487

concepts.label: Illusion of explanatory depth
concepts.learning_takeaway: Trying to explain a mechanism can reveal gaps hidden by an initial feeling of understanding.

relations.note: The authors identify the explanatory-knowledge illusion as a metacognitive problem and test changes in self-ratings of understanding.

concepts.card: In an observational treatment study, people classified as treated may need to survive from cohort entry until treatment begins. Misassigning that pre-treatment period to the treated group can create an apparent survival advantage unrelated to the treatment's effect.

evidence.locator: Immortal time bias; lines 204-206
evidence.note: Survival required before exposure assignment can produce spurious benefit.

concepts.label: Immortal time bias
concepts.learning_takeaway: Survival needed to receive an exposure can create a misleading apparent treatment advantage.

relations.note: Source explicitly defines bias through cohort-entry and intervention timing.

concepts.card: Inattentional blindness occurs when an unexpected visible event escapes awareness while attention is directed elsewhere. In Simons and Chabris’s counting task, some observers missed a conspicuous person crossing the scene. Detection varied with what observers attended to.

evidence.locator: Abstract and Introduction, PDF pp. 1-2, lines 32-56; Procedures and Results, PDF pp. 8-11

concepts.label: Inattentional blindness
concepts.learning_takeaway: Attention to a monitoring task can leave a visible unexpected event unnoticed.

relations.note: The original authors explicitly study inattentional blindness as a form of visual perception without focused attention.

concepts.card: Takuo Itoh’s 1995 furisode kimono demonstrates shibori at the scale of an entire garment. A continuous dyed pattern crosses the back seam and extends from body to sleeves. Planning on fabric of fixed width aligns areas that garment construction later joins.

evidence.locator: Curatorial description, lines 10–12; object identification, 31–39

concepts.label: Tokuseu Hitome Sohshibori Hon Furisode (Met 1997.228)
concepts.learning_takeaway: Trace a planned dye pattern across garment seams.

relations.note: The museum explicitly identifies this garment’s shibori technique.

aliases: Peremptory norms of general international law
concepts.card: Jus cogens denotes peremptory norms accepted by the international community of states as a whole, permitting no derogation. Under Vienna Convention Article 53, a treaty conflicting with such a norm when concluded is void; ordinary agreement cannot override it.

evidence.locator: Article 53, printed page 17

concepts.label: Jus cogens
concepts.learning_takeaway: Recognize limits on treaty agreement.

relations.note: Peremptory norms constrain international law.

concepts.card: Kanoko shibori is a resist dyeing method that binds small pinches of cloth before dyeing. Releasing the ties produces tiny undyed details, often squares with central dots. A Met robe illustrates how many individually tied units create an extensive patterned surface.

evidence.locator: Curatorial description, lines 10–11; Artwork Details

concepts.label: Kanoko shibori
concepts.learning_takeaway: Connect individual bindings with a repeated dot pattern.

relations.note: The Met describes kanoko as a shibori variant.

concepts.card: Khipus recorded information in the Inca Empire through cords and knots. Knot positions can represent decimal places, while twists, attachments, and colors provide further distinctions whose meanings scholars investigate. Numerical organization therefore depends on a cord’s structure, rather than an alphabetic sequence of written words.

evidence.locator: What is a khipu?; Encoding the Khipu; Khipu Uses, lines 132–157 and 195

concepts.label: Khipu
concepts.learning_takeaway: Read decimal organization in knots while retaining interpretive uncertainty.

relations.note: NIST documents khipu use throughout the Inca Empire.

concepts.card: Kintsugi is the Japanese art of repairing broken ceramics with gold lacquer. The repair restores function while giving damage a visible artistic role. The Met interprets this treatment as enhancing a prized object’s value, a curatorial judgment rather than a universal price rule.

evidence.locator: Exhibition overview, lines 10–11

concepts.label: Kintsugi
concepts.learning_takeaway: Understand visible repair as an artistic treatment of damage.

relations.note: The exhibition identifies kintsugi within Japanese ceramic art.

concepts.card: Kleptoplasty is a symbiosis in which an animal retains chloroplasts taken from algal food. In Elysia chlorotica, these plastids remain in digestive cells and continue photosynthesis; the slug retains chloroplasts rather than complete algal cells.

evidence.locator: Abstract; Introduction; Figure 1; lines 143-173

concepts.label: Kleptoplasty
concepts.learning_takeaway: An animal can retain algal chloroplasts without retaining a complete algal cell.

relations.note: Introduction explicitly identifies plastid symbiosis.

concepts.card: A koan is a paradoxical question that a Zen teacher gives a student for meditation. Its purpose is to interrupt habitual analytical thinking rather than supply an ordinary explanatory answer. The tradition treats this encounter as a possible route toward realization.

evidence.locator: Definition, line 56

concepts.label: Koan
concepts.learning_takeaway: Distinguish a contemplative question from an explanatory answer.

relations.note: Zen meditation context motivates this Buddhist practice placement.

concepts.card: Kotekan is an interlocking technique in Balinese gamelan. Two musicians divide rapid melodic figures into separate parts whose combination maintains rhythmic continuity. The result belongs to the composition’s melody: listening to either player alone misses the continuous composite line.

evidence.locator: Paragraph 2.2, lines 67–70

concepts.label: Kotekan
concepts.learning_takeaway: Hear the composite melody across paired parts.

relations.note: Tenzer identifies kotekan within Balinese gamelan texture.

concepts.card: Kulintang Kultura honors musician and teacher Danongan Kalanduyan through two contrasting discs. His ensemble performs traditional Philippine gong music on the first; diaspora artists combine kulintang with contemporary genres on the second. Their juxtaposition makes musical inheritance and transformation audible within one collection.

evidence.locator: Album description, lines 456–457; Release Info, 505–513

concepts.label: Kulintang Kultura: Danongan Kalanduyan and Gong Music of the Philippine Diaspora
concepts.learning_takeaway: Compare inheritance and transformation across the album’s discs.

relations.note: The album documents traditional and diaspora kulintang music.

concepts.card: Kulintang is a gong chime music tradition of the Philippines. The Kulintang Kultura album contrasts traditional ensemble repertoire with diaspora musicians’ combinations of kulintang and electronic, hip hop, rock and jazz styles. Hearing both reveals preservation through changing musical arrangements.

evidence.locator: Lesson introduction and learning objectives, lines 440–455
Album description, lines 456–457
evidence.note: Traditional and contemporary repertoire comparison inspected.

concepts.label: Kulintang music
concepts.learning_takeaway: Compare traditional repertoire with diaspora adaptations.

relations.note: The lesson identifies kulintang as Philippine gong chime music.

concepts.card: Kundiman is a Filipino song form in triple meter. In Felipe De Leon’s account, flowing melodies and subtle second beat syncopation loosen the beat’s pull. Devotion can address a partner, family, spiritual figure or motherland, extending the form beyond romantic love.

evidence.locator: Essay adaptation, lines 68–78

concepts.label: Kundiman
concepts.learning_takeaway: Connect triple meter and melodic flow with devotion.

relations.note: The essay identifies kundiman as a musical form.

concepts.card: LAGEOS is a pair of passive satellites covered with reflecting prisms. Laser measurements to these orbiting targets help investigate Earth's motion and shape, including plate movement and rotation. The satellites carry no electronics or sensors: their role is to provide stable reflective targets.

evidence.locator: LAGEOS 1 & 2 overview; lines 235-258
evidence.note: Passive reflecting satellite pair supports laser geodesy.

concepts.label: LAGEOS
concepts.learning_takeaway: Passive reflecting satellites provide long-lived laser targets for measuring Earth's motion and shape.

relations.note: NASA explicitly identifies a pair of orbiting satellites.

concepts.card: Leaf area index compares green leaf surface with ground area. For broadleaf plants it uses one leaf side; for conifers it uses half the total needle surface. This canopy measure helps model photosynthesis and exchanges of water, energy and carbon.

evidence.locator: Leaf Area Index definition and uses; lines 50-54
evidence.note: Leaf-surface ratio and plant-process modeling uses are explicit.

concepts.label: Leaf area index
concepts.learning_takeaway: Normalize leaf surface by ground area to describe canopy structure and model vegetation processes.

relations.note: Canopy and plant-process premises support editorial plant-physiology placement.

concepts.card: Cancer screening disproportionately detects slower-growing cancers because they remain detectable before symptoms for longer. This length-time bias changes the mix of cancers found. More early-stage diagnoses can therefore occur without establishing that screening reduces deaths; detection patterns alone do not show the benefit.

evidence.locator: Length bias and overdiagnosis; lines 34-38
evidence.note: Longer preclinical windows enrich slower cancers and distort benefit measures.

concepts.label: Length-time bias in cancer screening
concepts.learning_takeaway: Screening preferentially detects slower-growing cancers with longer preclinical windows.

relations.note: Source explicitly explains the bias in cancer screening.

concepts.card: L’Estampe Originale was a print portfolio issued in nine installments from 1893 to 1895. Its range of media depended on collaboration between artists and professional printers. These partnerships enabled technical experiments, making the printer’s expertise part of artistic production.

evidence.locator: Curatorial article, lines 13–16, 22, 31–38

concepts.label: L’Estampe Originale
concepts.learning_takeaway: Connect artistic experimentation with professional printers’ expertise.

relations.note: The portfolio collected collaborative experimental printmaking.

concepts.card: Under FIVB 2025–2028 rules, the Libero replaces back-row players through special replacement procedures. The role cannot serve or block, and cannot complete an attack when the ball is entirely above the net at contact. Defensive specialization therefore comes with defined playing restrictions.

evidence.locator: 19.3.1, printed p. 42 / PDF p. 44; 19.3.2.1-2, printed p. 43 / PDF p. 45

concepts.label: Libero in volleyball
concepts.learning_takeaway: A back-row specialist has distinct replacement rights and attacking, blocking and serving limits.

relations.note: FIVB Rule 19 defines the Libero’s role, playing actions and replacements within volleyball.

concepts.card: This Luba memory board communicates through incised designs and relief carving, whereas many other lukasa use attached beads and shells. The Met’s interpretation connects its motifs with political history and territory. Senior Mbudye members learned to decipher the board within a specialized knowledge tradition.

evidence.locator: Curatorial description, lines 10–16; Artwork Details, object number 1977.467.3

concepts.label: Lukasa memory board (Met 1977.467.3)
concepts.learning_takeaway: Examine how this carved board supports trained historical interpretation.

concepts.card: In matching-market unraveling, participants arrange appointments progressively earlier to get ahead of competitors. Contracts can be signed before candidates’ qualifications or employers’ needs are clear. Roth and Xing’s historical examples show how this timing race can thin later opportunities.

evidence.locator: Introduction, lines 87-91 and 146-164; I. Unraveling in a prototypical market, lines 177-197

concepts.label: Unraveling in matching markets
concepts.learning_takeaway: Competition to secure matches can push offers earlier, before useful information becomes available.

relations.note: Editorial bridge to stable matching: the authors distinguish appointment-date instability from blocking-pair instability and discuss centralized match procedures.

concepts.card: In Maximum Score golf, the committee sets a cap on the score for each hole. A player who does not finish the hole still receives that capped score. The format remains stroke play while bounding the contribution of a difficult hole.
concepts.label: Maximum Score golf
concepts.learning_takeaway: A committee-set cap limits each hole’s stroke score, including holes not finished.

relations.note: Capped stroke totals differ from Stableford points and scoring in sport generally.

concepts.card: Mbudye is a Luba association charged with preserving and interpreting political and historical principles. Its councils could check or reinforce chiefly power. Members progressed through levels of knowledge, with those at the highest level authorized to interpret the intricate designs of lukasa memory boards.

evidence.locator: Curatorial description, lines 12–14

concepts.label: Mbudye association
concepts.learning_takeaway: Connect specialized historical knowledge with checks on chiefly power.

relations.note: Editorial placement based on the association’s documented Luba state role.

concepts.card: The McGurk effect occurs when conflicting heard and seen speech can produce a perceived syllable present in neither input. Auditory ba paired with visual ga can be heard as da. Responses vary across listeners and stimuli, showing variability in audiovisual speech integration.

evidence.locator: Abstract and Introduction, PDF pp. 1-2, lines 8-28 and 63-80

concepts.label: McGurk effect
concepts.learning_takeaway: Mismatched heard and seen syllables can produce a perceived syllable present in neither input.

relations.note: The paper characterizes a perceptual speech illusion; perception is a general editorial parent.

concepts.card: Membership closure occurs when someone joins an activity or organization through a friend’s existing affiliation. The added edge connects person and focus. In a social-affiliation network, existing friendships can therefore help shape new memberships.

evidence.locator: 4.3, Co-Evolution of Social and Affiliation Networks, PDF pp. 12-13, lines 375-402

concepts.label: Membership closure
concepts.learning_takeaway: An existing friendship can lead to a new affiliation.

relations.note: Friendship can create a person-to-focus membership edge.

concepts.card: A Merkle consistency proof connects an earlier tree root to a larger tree root through intermediate hashes. It establishes that the earlier leaves remain an unchanged prefix, supporting append-only history. This checks continuity between trees rather than one leaf’s membership.
concepts.label: Merkle consistency proof
concepts.learning_takeaway: Intermediate hashes establish that a larger tree preserves an earlier tree’s unchanged prefix.

relations.note: Append-only prefix preservation differs from leaf membership and general cryptography.

concepts.card: A Merkle inclusion proof supplies the sibling hashes needed to recompute a tree’s root from one leaf. Matching an authenticated root establishes that leaf’s membership under the hash assumptions. It proves inclusion, rather than preservation of the entire earlier tree.
concepts.label: Merkle inclusion proof
concepts.learning_takeaway: An authentication path recomputes a root to establish one leaf’s membership in a tree.

relations.note: One-leaf membership differs from append-only consistency; cryptography is the broad parent.

concepts.card: Metaphysical grounding asks what makes a fact hold in virtue of another, rather than what caused it earlier. Philosophers use picketing as constituting a strike to illustrate the distinction. The disputed notion concerns constitutive explanation or determination, not just a necessary connection.

evidence.locator: Introduction, lines 13–18; §1.1 Determination and explanation

concepts.label: Metaphysical grounding
concepts.learning_takeaway: Separate constitutive dependence from causal history.

relations.note: The entry explicitly locates grounding questions within metaphysics.

concepts.card: Moral hazard in teams arises when individual actions are hidden but joint output is observable. In Holmström’s model, sharing that output under a balanced budget can leave members with incentives to free ride. The team setting changes the contract-design problem.

evidence.locator: Abstract and Introduction, printed pp.324-325 / PDF pp.2-3; free-rider discussion, printed p.325 / PDF p.3

concepts.label: Moral hazard in teams
concepts.learning_takeaway: Shared observable output with hidden individual actions creates a team-specific free-riding problem.

relations.note: The introduction explicitly defines the paper’s setting as a multiagent extension of the moral-hazard problem.

concepts.card: A multitask incentive model treats effort as attention allocated across different duties. When duties compete for that attention, rewarding easily measured output can divert effort from valuable work that is harder to measure. The effect depends on task substitution and measurement.

evidence.locator: Introduction, printed pp. 24-26 / PDF pages 1-2, distinguishing mark and competing-attention paragraphs

concepts.label: Multitask incentive problem
concepts.learning_takeaway: Rewarding measurable output can shift effort away from other valuable duties competing for attention.

relations.note: The introduction explicitly contrasts multidimensional principal-agent models with one-dimensional models.

concepts.card: Muon tomography uses scattering of naturally occurring cosmic-ray muons to reconstruct three-dimensional images of hidden material. Tracking changes in particle paths provides the information without adding an artificial radiation dose. Long exposures, limited position resolution and complex reconstruction remain practical challenges.

evidence.locator: Abstract; lines 15-17
evidence.note: Coulomb scattering enables natural-flux imaging with stated limitations.

concepts.label: Muon tomography
concepts.learning_takeaway: Natural muon scattering can reveal dense hidden structures without an added artificial radiation source.

relations.note: Source explicitly uses muon paths and scattering for imaging.

concepts.card: Mutual exclusivity is a word-learning default that discourages assigning an unfamiliar label to an already named whole object. It can guide a learner toward an unnamed object or property. Context can override the assumption; objects may legitimately have multiple names.

evidence.locator: Mutual Exclusivity, printed pp. 140-141 / PDF pp. 4-5; Constraints as Default Assumptions, pp. 142-145

concepts.label: Mutual exclusivity in word learning
concepts.learning_takeaway: An unfamiliar label can be assigned to an unnamed object or property instead of a familiar whole object.

relations.note: The authors explicitly treat mutual exclusivity as a proposed constraint guiding children’s acquisition of word meanings.

concepts.card: Nafion is a named family of fluorinated polymer membranes used in electrochemical applications. Its sulfonic membranes are based on a perfluorosulfonic-acid and PTFE copolymer and conduct positively charged ions. The membrane's polymer composition is tied to its role inside electrochemical cells.

evidence.locator: Membranes for a Wide Variety of Electrochemical Applications; lines 151-153; grades tables
evidence.note: Manufacturer identifies copolymer basis and cation conduction.

concepts.label: Nafion
concepts.learning_takeaway: A named fluorinated polymer membrane family conducts cations in electrochemical cells.

relations.note: Manufacturer explicitly identifies a polymer membrane family.

concepts.card: Natural Earth is a compromise world-map projection with rounded corners. It preserves neither areas nor angles exactly. High-latitude regions appear enlarged, while angular distortion increases toward the edges, showing why an attractive general-purpose map still requires care when comparing regions.

evidence.locator: Description; Distortion; Limitations

concepts.label: Natural Earth projection
concepts.learning_takeaway: Recognize distortion within a rounded world-map compromise.

relations.note: Esri identifies Natural Earth as a world-map projection.

concepts.card: Negative pressure wound therapy uses a sealed dressing connected to a suction pump. Removing wound fluid and reducing swelling can support healing. Clinicians select suitable wounds for this treatment; the intended outcome does not make the device appropriate for every wound.

evidence.locator: Definition and mechanism; lines 50-76; indications and contraindications, lines 78-104
evidence.note: Sealed-dressing suction removes fluid and reduces swelling.

concepts.label: Negative pressure wound therapy
concepts.learning_takeaway: Controlled suction removes wound fluid while a sealed dressing supports healing.

relations.note: Provider-directed treatment supports editorial placement under medicine.
Source identifies wound healing as the intended outcome.

concepts.card: Published between 1936 and 1966, with a wartime interruption, the Green Book listed businesses welcoming African American travelers. Reports from readers and postal-worker contacts helped build its directory. Hotels, restaurants, and service stations turned shared local knowledge into a practical response to segregation.

evidence.locator: Publication and directory history, lines 24–35

concepts.label: The Negro Motorist Green Book
concepts.learning_takeaway: Trace how shared information supported travel under segregation.

relations.note: Editorial historical placement based on the documented segregation context.

concepts.card: Nembutsu is a Buddhist chanting practice. At the Buddhist Temple of Marin, a Jodo Shinshu community, chanting Namo Amida Butsu expresses gratitude. The temple places this chant alongside listening and compassionate living, illustrating a devotional function within one specific Buddhist tradition.

evidence.locator: Tradition statement and practices, lines 118, 145–165

concepts.label: Nembutsu
concepts.learning_takeaway: Recognize gratitude as the chant’s described devotional function.

relations.note: The temple identifies Nembutsu within its Buddhist practices.

concepts.card: NIST SRM 610 is a trace-element glass reference material. A piece aboard NASA's Perseverance rover helps calibrate PIXL, an instrument that measures elements in Martian rocks. A characterized Earth material supplies a reference for interpreting measurements made on another planet.

evidence.locator: PIXL calibration discussion; lines 126-130
evidence.note: Glass reference material calibrates Perseverance's PIXL.

concepts.label: NIST SRM 610
concepts.learning_takeaway: Characterized trace-element glass can calibrate elemental measurements on Mars.

relations.note: Calibration premises support an editorial metrology application.
Source explicitly identifies SRM 610 as glass.

concepts.card: Nixtamalization cooks and steeps maize in an alkaline solution, commonly containing food-grade lime (calcium hydroxide). Washing and milling turn the kernels into dough for foods such as tortillas. Lime cooking increases calcium content; processing also makes niacin more available.

concepts.card: Non-refoulement protects people against return to prohibited danger. concepts.card: A nonunion is a broken bone that fails to heal, rather than a fracture that is merely healing slowly. Bone repair depends on stability, blood supply and nutrition. The distinction requires clinical and imaging context; it is not defined by one universal waiting period.

concepts.card: Oblivious HTTP sends encrypted requests through a relay to a gateway. The relay sees the client but cannot read the request; the gateway decrypts it but sees the relay. Privacy depends on separated knowledge, including those parties not colluding.

concepts.card: Occultation for weed control uses an opaque cover to block light over a garden bed. Warmth and moisture can encourage seeds to sprout, while darkness prevents the seedlings from sustaining growth. Weather and site conditions affect how the process performs.

concepts.card: Ottava rima organizes a stanza into eight lines rhyming abababcc, usually in iambic pentameter. After six lines alternate two rhymes, the closing couplet introduces a paired ending. The form can carry longer poems, including Byron’s Don Juan.

concepts.card: P-factor is asymmetric propeller loading at a high angle of attack. The blades experience unequal relative airflow, shifting the effective center of thrust away from the shaft. This creates a yawing tendency whose direction depends on propeller rotation.

concepts.card: This late-thirteenth-century Yuan safe-conduct pass carries an imperial inscription in Phakpa script. concepts.card: Pansori is a Korean narrative vocal genre performed by one singer and one drummer. The singer develops an epic story through poetic, dramatic and musical expression. Sugungga illustrates how this small performing partnership can carry an extended tale with multiple characters.

concepts.card: Photobleaching irreversibly removes a fluorescent molecule's ability to emit light through photochemical destruction during illumination. concepts.card: A polymer's properties can change through structural recovery, a process called physical aging. This affects viscoelastic behavior and engineering properties. concepts.card: Pinpeat is Cambodia’s court music tradition. Smithsonian’s diaspora lesson asks how Cambodian American artists sustain and transform it in the United States. Studying both settings shows how cultural preservation can include adaptation as musicians encounter new social contexts.

concepts.card: Preferential attachment is a rule in which well-connected nodes are more likely to receive new links. Repeated growth can amplify an initial advantage, producing a few highly connected nodes. This is a simplified network model, not a universal explanation of popularity.

concepts.card: In Kapur’s 2006 study, student groups initially struggled with ill-structured problems without scaffolding. concepts.card: A pycnocline is an ocean layer where density increases rapidly with depth. This stable density gradient can restrict exchange between surface and deeper water. Temperature, salinity or both may contribute, so a density boundary need not match one single temperature or salt boundary.

concepts.card: QPACK compresses HTTP/3 field sections using a shared dynamic table and separate instruction streams. Referring to a table entry that has not arrived can block decoding. Limiting blocked streams trades compression reuse against the cost of waiting.

concepts.card: Odilon Redon’s 1895 lithograph The Buddha appeared in the ninth L’Estampe Originale album. Printed using chine collé, it combines black ink with light gray paper. The Met’s account shows how the paper itself contributes the image’s cool background tone.

concepts.card: After malnutrition, restarting nutrition can trigger dangerous electrolyte shifts as carbohydrate metabolism resumes. evidence.note: Renewed metabolism shifts electrolytes into cells after malnutrition.

concepts.card: Relative performance evaluation lets a contract use peers’ outcomes alongside an agent’s own performance. concepts.label: Relative performance evaluation
concepts.learning_takeaway: Peers’ outcomes can supply information useful for designing an individual’s incentive contract.

concepts.card: A root hair is a slender extension of a root epidermal cell, with its wall and membrane projecting into the surrounding growing medium. Water and nutrients enter through these fine outgrowths, connecting the root's surface to its supply.

concepts.card: A runway incursion is an incorrect presence of an aircraft, vehicle or person in the protected area of a surface designated for aircraft landing and takeoff. The FAA safety category describes an occurrence, including cases without immediate collision consequences.

concepts.card: Sanké Môn is an annual collective fishing ritual in San, Mali, commemorating the town’s foundation. concepts.card: Saturation flow rate describes the hourly rate at which a queued lane could discharge under continuous green with no lost time. It is a reference flow: an actual signal cycle allocates only some of its time to effective green.

concepts.learning_takeaway: Continuous-green discharge with no lost time is a reference rate, distinct from actual signal capacity.

concepts.card: In Schelling’s simplified two-group models, people move when local neighbors fail their tolerance threshold. evidence.note: Glossary defines area between stitching and raw edge.

concepts.card: Sentinel lymph node biopsy identifies and samples the first node or nodes most likely to receive cancer spreading from a tumor. Examining them helps stage the cancer. A negative result suggests no spread to nearby nodes, but cannot guarantee it.

evidence.note: Selected first nodes are removed and examined for cancer spread.

concepts.label: Shikantaza

concepts.learning_takeaway: Compare a compressed form with its sestina model.

relations.note: The Academy explicitly calls tritina a contraction of sestina.

concepts.card: Truthmaker maximalism claims that every truth requires something in the world to make it true. The strain appears with negative truths: if absolutely nothing existed, what could make that true? This challenges the doctrine unless one rejects the possibility of an empty world.

evidence.locator: §2.1 Maximalism, lines 181–203

concepts.label: Truthmaker maximalism
concepts.learning_takeaway: Test a universal truthmaker requirement against negative truths.

relations.note: The entry identifies maximalism as a position within truthmaker theory.

concepts.card: Truthmaker theory asks how true representations depend on reality. A truthmaker must be relevant to what a claim is about, rather than merely entail it. What sits behind a refrigerator, for example, cannot explain why a truth of arithmetic holds.

evidence.locator: §1.1 Truthmaking as Entailment, relevance discussion; §1.2, lines 66–85

concepts.label: Truthmaker theory
concepts.learning_takeaway: Connect truth to relevant reality rather than mere entailment.

relations.note: The entry explicitly treats truthmaking as a metaphysical project.

concepts.card: Color every positive integer using finitely many colors. Van der Waerden's theorem says that, for any chosen finite length, some arithmetic progression has that many terms all in one color. Regular spacing must emerge somewhere despite the coloring's freedom.

evidence.locator: Four equivalent formulations; lines 13-19
evidence.note: Finite colorings force monochromatic arithmetic progressions.

concepts.label: van der Waerden's theorem
concepts.learning_takeaway: Finite colorings of the positive integers force arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions.

relations.note: Finite-color combinatorial existence supports editorial combinatorics placement.

concepts.card: Vaucheria litorea is the alga eaten by Elysia chlorotica in its plastid partnership. Its chloroplasts enter the slug's digestive cells, while other algal organelles are not retained. The food organism supplies photosynthetic machinery without becoming a whole-cell resident.

evidence.locator: Abstract; Introduction; Figure 1; lines 143-173
evidence.note: Algal food supplies only the retained plastids.

concepts.label: Vaucheria litorea
concepts.learning_takeaway: This algal prey supplies the chloroplasts retained by Elysia chlorotica.

relations.note: Introduction explicitly identifies algal food.

concepts.card: Voice onset time measures the timing between a stop consonant’s release and the start of vocal-fold vibration. Voicing that begins before release gives a negative value. This timing dimension helps distinguish speech sounds without requiring one universal boundary between phonemes.

evidence.locator: Legacy: Abramson/Lisker VOT Stimuli, definition and synthesized continuum, lines 21-27

concepts.label: Voice onset time
concepts.learning_takeaway: Timing between stop release and vocal-fold vibration distinguishes speech sounds.

relations.note: The laboratory explicitly presents VOT as an acoustic phonetic measure introduced to characterize stop-consonant voicing distinctions.

concepts.card: A rotational fault occurs when a volleyball team serves out of order. Under FIVB 2025–2028 rules, the order must be corrected and the opponent receives a point and next serve. The faulty team’s subsequent points are cancelled only if the fault’s start can be determined.

evidence.locator: 7.7 Rotational Fault, printed p. 26 / PDF p. 28

concepts.label: Volleyball rotational fault
concepts.learning_takeaway: Serving out of rotation is a service-order fault with a correction and specified scoring consequences.

relations.note: The named fault is one of the official game rules for volleyball service order.

concepts.card: Wearing ease is room beyond body measurements that a garment pattern includes for comfortable wear. Extra fullness chosen to change the garment's style is separately called design ease, serving a different purpose.

evidence.locator: Wearing versus design ease; fabric edges; lines 84, 154, 178
evidence.note: Comfort allowance differs from additional style fullness.

concepts.label: Wearing ease
concepts.learning_takeaway: Comfort room built into a pattern differs from extra room chosen for style.

relations.note: Guide explicitly defines a sewing-pattern component.

concepts.card: Wheelchair tennis permits a player to return the ball after a second bounce. The first bounce must still satisfy the ordinary court-boundary rule; the second may land outside the court. The adaptation changes return timing while preserving the first-bounce requirement.

evidence.locator: Rules of Wheelchair Tennis a. The Two Bounce Rule, printed p.16 / PDF p.19, lines 565-571; ordinary boundary Rules 24(c)-25, printed pp.10-11 / PDF pp.13-14, lines 363-364 and 414-430

concepts.label: Wheelchair tennis two-bounce rule
concepts.learning_takeaway: A wheelchair player may return after two bounces, and the second bounce may fall outside the court.

relations.note: The Rules of Wheelchair Tennis explicitly introduce exceptions to the ITF Rules of Tennis.

concepts.card: The whole-object assumption is an initial hypothesis in word learning: a new label for an object names the object as a whole. It narrows possible meanings among parts, substances and properties, but other linguistic and contextual cues can override it.

evidence.locator: The Taxonomic and Whole Object Assumptions, printed p. 139 / PDF p. 3, lines 79-85; default-bias qualification, p. 145 / PDF p. 9, lines 274-299

concepts.label: Whole-object assumption in word learning
concepts.learning_takeaway: A new object label is initially interpreted as naming the whole object rather than its parts or material.

relations.note: The paper explicitly defines it as one of the biases used by children to constrain possible meanings during word learning.

concepts.card: The wrong kind of reason problem challenges certain fitting-attitude theories of value. A demon’s threat might give someone reason to value a worthless cup of mud. The incentive concerns having the attitude, while leaving the object’s value unexplained; theories must distinguish these reasons.

evidence.locator: §3.1 The Wrong Kind of Reason Problem, lines 167–175

concepts.label: Wrong kind of reason problem
concepts.learning_takeaway: Separate reasons to adopt an attitude from an object’s value.

relations.note: The entry explicitly identifies this challenge to fitting-attitude theories.
